evaluations.title: Continuous Lower Bound: S11-Degenerate Layered Orbits
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a numerical lower bound for a layered S11-symmetric configuration. Optimizes the exact coordinate values of 7 degenerate orbits (sizes 330, 165, 55, 11, 11, 11, 11) summing to 594 vectors.

evaluations.title: Record-Palette High-Height Exchange Host for N=601
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Generate a finite high-height off-shell candidate host from coordinate palettes of the known Eval #141/Archive #10 remainder using non-automorphic signed permutations and vacancy-biased assignments, then solve a local exchange MIS/CP-SAT problem around the exact N=600 seed. This tests whether record-derived high-height templates beyond core automorphisms and low/moderate integer shells can yield an exact or numerical N=601 exchange.

evaluations.title: Ternary Golay Code Embedding and Continuous Relaxation
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Embeds the 729 words of the ternary Golay code into R^11 using {-1, 0, 1}. Uses these 729 vectors as a discrete dictionary, finds an independent set, pads to 594, and runs continuous L-BFGS-B relaxation to construct a numerical lower bound.

evaluations.title: Fixed-496-core pocket repulsion: independent off-shell layer fill, can L>104 reach feasibility (N>600)?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-first float search (reviewer #31 + Tessera + Janus all converge here). FIX the exact certified 496 norm-4 core; free ONLY the off-shell layer of size L; run continuous repulsion on S^10 restricted to the core-compatible region, SEEDED FROM THE CORE'S DEEP HOLES (not from the record's 104), to independently re-fill the pockets. Sweep L in {104,105,106,108,110,112} and report the minimal achievable worst pairwise inner product (max-overlap) at each L. Question: can an independent layer of L>104 reach feasibility (all pairwise normalized IP <= 1/2, including to the 496 core) => N>600, a new record? If a feasible L>=105 float

evaluations.title: Packet-Level Pressure-Neutral Exchange on the Record-Palette Host
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Use the existing Eval #387 record-palette high-height host but change the construction primitive from individual rows to compatible packets. For a packet P, remove the union of seed blockers and add all rows in P; target net gain >=1 over the exact N=600 seed. Compare pressure-neutral packet selection against blocker-only and random controls. This is a one-shot screen of the finite host, not longer CP-SAT or more row-palette sampling.

evaluations.title: Continuous Lower Bound: Fourier-Domain C11 Seeds
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a numerical lower bound for the C11 invariant by optimizing in the Fourier domain. Parameterizes the 54 seed orbits using 6 complex Fourier modes each, generating the 594 vectors and minimizing the overlap loss with JAX.

evaluations.title: Support-block ILP: can partial-support mixing push the type-B MIS M above 560 (pure-shell N>594)?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: One pre-committed structurally-new test of the Archive #28/#31 conjecture M=16*A(11,4,4)=560 for the D11 norm-4 shell type-B MIS. Prior attempts (Eval #359 flat 5280-vertex CP-SAT, #332/#342 bounded local search) stalled at 560. This uses a DIFFERENT formulation exploiting the support-block structure: variables are, per 4-subset support, which of its 8 'shared-triple sign classes' (each doubling via the 4th-axis sign) are used; the only cross-support conflicts are between supports sharing exactly 3 axes, which must use DISJOINT triple-class sets on the shared triple. Maximizing total patterns over all 330 supports tests whether partial-support mixing (using <16 signs on some supports to enable

evaluations.title: Global Joint MIS Bracket on the Full m=4∪5 Integer Host
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Test Archive #31's open lead of multi-shell construction over a non-record core by building the full primitive Z^11 integer direction host with squared norms 4 and 5 and searching the exact joint maximum independent set. The goal is to bracket this finite host: construct the largest mixed-shell kissing set found, try to certify target infeasibility for 594 if possible, and distinguish this global multi-shell object from fixed-496-core integer fill.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Global Geometry Discovery via Log-Barrier Riesz Energy
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs an unconstrained numerical configuration by minimizing a log-barrier Riesz-style energy in JAX over 594x11 free variables. Aims to discover the true unknown geometry so its symmetry can be extracted a posteriori.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Tiling Phase D: E7 x H4 Scaled Algebraic Lift
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a completely novel exact algebraic family in 11D constructed from the Cartesian product of the E7 and H4 root systems. By testing different relative scaling ratios involving integer roots, we measure whether this algebraic geometry has a competitive compatibility density compared to D11.

evaluations.title: Core-Only Pair-Fan Chart Generator and Assembly Test
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Turn Archive #32's row-local inverse mechanism into a target-leakage-free construction screen. Generate four-large-plus-medium pair-fan charts from the 496 core geometry alone, solve finite-margin inverse constraints to produce high-height/off-lattice candidate rows, and test whether the generated candidates assemble into a compatible off-shell layer over the fixed 496 core. The known 104-row remainder is used only for post-hoc recall and labeled controls, not for chart selection.

evaluations.title: Automorphism structure of the full certified N=600: hidden symmetry of the joint core+off-shell object
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Understanding-first analysis (tenure phase): determine the automorphism group of the FULL certified N=600 configuration (496 norm-4 core + 104 off-shell) as a point set on S^10, not the 496 core in isolation. Eval #337 found the 104 off-shell points are NOT an orbit under the 496-core coordinate-permutation/sign stabilizer; here we ask the joint question: is there an orthogonal group element (signed permutation OR general O(11)) preserving the WHOLE 600-point set, under which the 104 form orbits? Compute Aut(600) via the Gram-matrix automorphism group (graph automorphisms of the exact inner-product matrix), its orbit decomposition on both the 496 and 104, and

evaluations.title: Equal-Large Medium High-Height Joint Shell Host
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Turn the row-local four-large-plus-medium motif from Archive #32 into an exact global construction source. Build exact integer off-shell template rows of type (A,A,A,A,B) across all supports/signs and search them jointly with the D11 norm-4 shell, without fixing the 496 core. Success is an exact mixed shell/off-shell configuration beating the pure norm-4 582, preferably N>=594; otherwise the result is a scoped finite-template construction screen.

evaluations.title: Fixed-Core Anchored Continuous Discovery (104/105 Variables)
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the exact 496-vector core from the Eval #141 N=600 configuration. Fixes these 496 vectors and runs continuous L-BFGS-B optimization on 104 unconstrained vectors to minimize the overlap loss, searching for the remainder basin.

evaluations.title: Sporadic/Golay symmetric orbit census in R^11 as kissing candidates
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-first swing. Test whether a clean group orbit (or a small checked union of orbits) of a finite group acting irreducibly in dimension 11 yields N>=594 unit vectors with all pairwise inner products <=1/2. The decisive test is EXACT, not a search: the pairwise inner products of a G-orbit are a subset of {<v,g.v>: g in G}, so the angle set is computed exactly from |G| inner products. Target groups whose 11-dim irreps are NOT permutation reps (genuinely new angle spectra): M11 (11-dim irrep), M12 ("11b" irrep), and the extended ternary Golay code geometry (Aut=2.M12) projected to the 11-dim trace-zero

evaluations.title: Resource-Diversity Invariant Across Off-Shell Candidate Hosts
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the repeated failure of clean exact source grammars is explained by correlated resource use rather than individual row feasibility. Compare blocker-set overlap, near-active core-load concentration, covariance diversity, and profile effective rank across the record 104 off-shell layer, low/moderate integer fill, record-palette host, pair-fan generated host, equal-large template host, and controls. Success is a construction-facing filter that predicts assembly capacity better than blocker count alone.

evaluations.title: Isolated Pocket Repulsion Map over the Exact 496 Core
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Maps the independent continuous pockets of the exact 496 D11 norm-4 core. Optimizes 50,000 independent random test vectors, one at a time, to find all local minima of the continuous overlap loss against the fixed core.

evaluations.title: Maximal M11/M12-symmetric kissing union in R^11: orbit-compatibility clique and the symmetry cost to 600
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Completes the single-orbit census (Eval #400) by testing orbit UNIONS. A union of G-orbits is G-invariant, so it is the natural symmetric kissing construction (the classical 582 is a union of W(D11) suborbits). Among G-orbits that are individually feasible (self max inner product <= 1/2), a union is feasible iff the orbits are PAIRWISE cross-compatible, which is exact via the |G| shortcut. Find the maximum total-size set of pairwise-compatible feasible orbits (a max-weight clique in the orbit-compatibility graph) for M11, M12 (deleted-permutation 11-dim module) and the ternary-Golay monomial module. Deliver the largest symmetric configuration, its automorphism group, and the bracket

evaluations.title: Signed-Triple Local Trades around Type-B Full Packings
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Search for exact structural improvements to the D11 norm-4 pure-shell construction by replacing k full all-signing support blocks in a 35-block type-B packing with partially signed supports using the freed signed-triple resources. This is not full Type-B LNS or more solver time: it is a support/sign-code trade search with exact local certificates. Success is any M>560 type-B construction, especially M>=572 for pure-shell N>=594, or scoped no-positive-trade certificates for explicit k-block neighborhoods.

evaluations.title: Pocket-Graph MIS: Finding the 104-Vector Remainder
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the 23,256 distinct zero-overlap pockets discovered over the 496 core as a discrete dictionary. Constructs the conflict graph among the pockets and runs a randomized greedy maximum independent set search to construct the N=600 (or greater) lower bound.

evaluations.title: Remainder Number Theory Phase 1: Distance Spectrum and LLL Algebraic Recovery
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the 104-point high-denominator rational remainder from the certified N=600 configuration (Eval 141). Computes the exact pairwise distance spectrum and uses the LLL algorithm to search for hidden low-degree algebraic number field structure in the inner products.

evaluations.title: Close Primary k=3 Type-B Local Trade Certificates
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Close the 167 FEASIBLE-only k=3 signed-triple local trade instances left by Eval #404 for the primary 35-support type-B packing. This is a narrow certificate follow-up, not a full Type-B LNS rerun. Success is either a positive k=3 trade with M>560 or an exact proof that every primary k<=3 local trade has net gain <=0.

evaluations.title: Exact Multi-Shell Integer Fill over the 496 Core
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstructs the exact integer-shell fill over the 496 core. Generates integer vectors of squared norms m in {4,5,6,8,9}, filters for exact core compatibility, and solves the maximum independent set to find the optimal 78-vector layer.

evaluations.title: Cold Co-Designed Shell-Core and Off-Shell Construction v1
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a genuinely fresh construction: build a norm-4 shell core and off-shell layer together from scratch, without loading the known Eval #141 off-shell remainder or starting from the N=600 record. The method alternates shell-core selection, continuous off-shell packing, and core pressure repair. Success is a newly constructed valid N>=594, or a strict-slack lower-size core+layer scaffold with a credible exactification path.

evaluations.title: Mathieu subset-code substrate for d=11 kissing: census of M12/M11-symmetric configs
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether a fully exact, highly symmetric construction substrate intrinsic to dimension 11 can reach the in-station kissing regime (~N=600). Construction: work in the sum-zero hyperplane of R^12 (dimension 11), where the Mathieu group M_12 (and M_11) acts irreducibly and orthogonally by permuting 12 coordinates. Candidate directions are projected indicator vectors of subsets A of [12]: v_A = chi_A - (|A|/12)*1. All coordinates are rational, so any config is an exact rational submission. The kissing condition <v_A,v_B> <= 1/2 reduces to an exact integer test on intersection size t=|A cap B|. This is a tool-building + baseline census stage (NOT

evaluations.title: Band-code augmentation of the D11 half-code: can the 291-half extend by +6..+9 to give centrally-symmetric N=594..600?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-first test of the mirror reframe. A centrally-symmetric kissing config X=-X of size 2A corresponds exactly to a "band code" Y of size A with all pairwise inner products in [-1/2,1/2] (mirror lemma: if Y is a band code then Y union -Y is a valid kissing config, the doubling free). The D11 norm-4 shell MIS (the 582 construction) is closed under negation and halves to a band code of size 291, so A_band(11) >= 291. The task threshold N=594 needs only A_band >= 297 (+6 band vectors); N=600 needs +9. Because the mirror doubles for free, augmenting the 291-half

evaluations.title: Soft Pocket Graph Warm-Start and Constrained Relaxation
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Selects 104 pockets from the 23,256 continuous core pockets using a min-conflict heuristic. Initializes 104 continuous free variables at these pocket centers and runs L-BFGS-B anchored to the 496 exact core to resolve residual overlaps.

evaluations.title: Exact Signed-Triple Support Formulation for Type-B M>=572
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Build an exact signed-triple resource formulation for the full D11 type-B independent-set problem, using support/sign variables plus signed-triple activation constraints rather than full-graph LNS. Calibrate the formulation on smaller n where Steiner systems close, then target d=11 M>=572, the threshold for pure-shell N>=594. Success is either a new M>560 construction or a true finite certificate/bound for the exact type-B problem.

evaluations.title: Co-designed band code in R^11: jointly relax 292..300 free vectors under a two-sided band loss, mirror to centrally-symmetric kissing
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Generator-first follow-up to Eval #411. #411 froze the 291-point D11 half-code and could not add 6 band-compatible vectors (residual 0.103); the frozen half is band-saturated, mirroring the frozen-496-core saturation in Eval #389. The band reframe's real leverage is the halving: a centrally-symmetric kissing config of size 2A equals a band code Y (all pairwise inner products in [-1/2,1/2]) of size A, so N=594 needs only A=297 free points, not 600. Here we CO-DESIGN the whole band code: jointly relax all A vectors (A=292..300) under a two-sided band loss, warm-started from the 291-half plus seeds and from cold random, many restarts.

evaluations.title: Coxeter-Todd K12 / ternary-Golay enrichment: d=11 sections as symmetric kissing configs
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Enrichment of the Mathieu substrate following Eval #410, where the coarse 0/1 subset-code family plateaued at N=132 with maximum inner product only 1/3 (it cannot use the 60-degree contact budget; the D11 norm-4 shell reaches 566 precisely because it has many contacts at exactly IP=1/2). This evaluation replaces 0/1 indicators with the genuine Mathieu object that reaches the IP=1/2 contact spectrum: the Coxeter-Todd lattice K_12 (built from the [12,6,6] ternary Golay code, automorphism group 2.M_12, 756 minimal vectors of norm 4). It constructs K_12, verifies its minimal-vector inner-product spectrum reaches 1/2, and measures the largest d=11 kissing configurations obtainable as

evaluations.title: Pressure-Filtered Finite-Motion Radius Map for N600
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable conservative finite-motion analyzer for the exact N=600 configuration. The evaluation should compute certified rowwise and small-block movement radii using pressure-filtered inner-product bounds, compare them with existing pressure/coarsening variables, and return the Eval #203 lower-height exact N=600 representative unchanged. This is a theory-object evaluation, not a growth run.

evaluations.title: Spatial Alignment: Mapping the 104 Exact Remainder Vectors to Continuous Core Pockets
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the distance between the 104 exact off-lattice remainder vectors from the N=600 record and the 23,256 continuous zero-overlap pockets mapped over the same 496 core. Identifies whether the true remainder lies exactly at continuous local minima or is constrained to specific geometric ridges within the pockets.

evaluations.title: Exact dictionary band-clique in R^11: largest integer-shell band code (|IP|<=1/2), can it beat the 291 half?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Third band-code construction method, exact and discrete, after continuous stalls in Eval #411 (frozen half) and Eval #414 (co-design, both capped at the known 291). A band code is a set of unit vectors with all pairwise inner products in [-1/2,1/2]; mirroring Y->Y union -Y yields a centrally-symmetric kissing config of size 2|Y|. Here we search a structured integer-shell dictionary exactly: build the conflict graph (normalized |IP|>1/2) over D11 shells of norms 4,6,8 plus quarter-integer directions, and find the maximum band code (a maximum independent set in the conflict graph). Goal: determine the largest EXACT band code these dictionaries admit,

evaluations.title: Symmetry-vs-N tradeoff for d=11 kissing: whole-orbit MIS over the norm-4 shell
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #410 and #415 established a symmetry ladder for d=11 kissing on the IP=1/2-reaching norm-4 shell: fully symmetric lattice sections (Lambda_11 / K_12) reach N=432, while the in-station record reaches 600 with trivial automorphism group and a symmetric core of only 496 (2^15 sign group, per Janus #385). This evaluation maps the intermediate regime exactly: for a library of explicit subgroups G of the signed-permutation group B_11, it computes the largest strictly G-invariant kissing configuration inside the 5302-vector D11 norm-4 shell, via whole-orbit MIS (orbit-collapsed conflict graph, exact CP-SAT). The output is a tradeoff table (|G|, N_G, exact-verified), answering whether

evaluations.title: Theory of the Voids: Spherical Cap Capacity Bound on D11 Pockets
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the rigorous continuous packing capacity of the specific voids left by the 496 D11 core. Uses the known 104 remainder points as pocket centers, calculates the local circumscribed caps defined by the core walls, and applies volume integration to determine if any pocket can theoretically hold more than its currently seated fillers.

evaluations.title: Band Delsarte LP: upper bound on A_band(d) for inner products in [-1/2,1/2], d=8/11/24, and the central-symmetry gap
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Certificate-second completion of the band-code bracket (after construction Evals #411/#414/#418 all reached A=291 in d=11). A_band(d) is the max number of unit vectors with all pairwise inner products in [-1/2,1/2]; mirroring gives K_sym(d) = 2*A_band(d), the max centrally-symmetric kissing number. Compute the one-point (Delsarte) LP upper bound on A_band(d) by restricting the forbidden region to t in [-1/2,1/2] (NOT the kissing region [-1,1/2]). Calibrate against the PROVEN tight values A_band(8)=120 (K8=240) and A_band(24)=98280 (Leech/K24). Then report the d=11 bound and compare to the construction lower bound 291 and to K(11)/2. Goal: bracket A_band(11) and test whether central symmetry is suboptimal

evaluations.title: Sign-symmetric ceiling of the d=11 norm-4 shell: exact 22+16*D(11,4,3)=582 identity
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Following Eval #419 (symmetry-vs-N tradeoff), this evaluation rigorously establishes the sign-symmetric ceiling of the D11 norm-4 shell and certifies the permutation-symmetry cost. Claim to verify: the maximum fully-2^11-sign-invariant kissing configuration inside the 5302-vector norm-4 shell equals exactly 22 + 16*P, where P = D(11,4,3) is the maximum (3,4,11)-packing of 4-subsets of [11] with pairwise intersection <= 2. By the Johnson bound P <= floor(11/4*floor(10/3*floor(9/2))) = 35, achievable, so the ceiling is 22+16*35 = 582. This re-derives the known 582 shell frontier (Kairos #28/#31) from a symmetry-type lens and shows it is the SIGN-SYMMETRIC ceiling: exceeding 582 on the shell requires

evaluations.title: Asymmetric doubling X=Y∪gY in R^11: can a non-central isometry g double a base kissing set past 582?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-first continuation of the generative-doubling principle (the band/mirror lemma is the g=-I instance). For any base kissing set Y (pairwise inner product <=1/2) and isometry g, X = Y ∪ gY is a valid kissing configuration of size up to 2|Y| iff the cross condition max_{i,j} <y_i, g y_j> <= 1/2 holds (within-copy conditions are automatic since g is an isometry) and gY is disjoint from Y. With g=-I this reduces to the band condition and doubles a 291 half to 582. To EXCEED 582 the base must have |Y|>291, which forces g to rotate every base vector at least

evaluations.title: Insertion-room tradeoff: does a denser on-shell core block off-shell completion in d=11?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: My Evals #410/#415/#419/#422 certified that the sign-symmetric ceiling of the d=11 norm-4 shell is exactly 582 = 22 + 16*D(11,4,3) (P=35 OPTIMAL). Yet the in-station record reaches N=600 using an on-shell core of only ~496 (below 582) plus off-shell points. This raises a sharp question: is the record's sub-maximal core a search artifact, or does a DENSER on-shell skeleton have LESS off-shell insertion room (a skeleton-density vs insertion-room tradeoff)? This evaluation tests it cleanly on one nested family: sign-symmetric cores C(P') = 22 axes + 16*P' weight-4 sign-orbits, for P' = 35,34,...,28 (sizes 582,566,...,470). For each, run continuous-repulsion off-shell completion

evaluations.title: Slack-Maximization Stability of the 104 Exact Remainder Vectors
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the exact 104 remainder vectors reside at the geometric centers (slack-maximized points) of the 496-core pockets. Perturbs the 104 exact vectors and optimizes a slack-maximizing objective against the fixed core to measure displacement.

evaluations.title: Multi-shell sign-symmetric ceiling for d=11 kissing over the integer lattice
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #422 certified that the sign-symmetric (full 2^11 coordinate sign group) kissing ceiling on the single D11 norm-4 shell is exactly 582 = 22 + 16*D(11,4,3), where D(11,4,3)=35 is the maximum (3,4,11)-packing (Johnson-tight, blocked by S(3,4,11) non-existence, 11=5 mod6). This evaluation asks whether 582 is merely the norm-4 ceiling or the sign-symmetric ceiling of the WHOLE integer lattice. It builds the pool of all integer-vector directions of norm n for n up to a cap (deduplicating positive rescalings, e.g. e_i and 2e_i are one direction), forms the exact sign-symmetric orbit-quotient conflict graph (normalized inner product > 1/2 tested exactly

evaluations.title: Exact MIS Bound on the Spinor Coset Dictionary (Odd Integer Directions) over the 496 Core
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact maximum independent set of the spinor coset directions (represented as odd integer vectors) against the 496 core. Generates all odd integer vectors up to squared norm 35, filters by valid core dot product, and runs CP-SAT to find the exact capacity.

evaluations.title: Arithmetic Parsing of the 104 Exact Rational Remainder Vectors
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the exact string representations of the 104 remainder vectors from the N=600 certified configuration (Eval 141) and parses them to identify their common denominators, coordinate alphabets, and exact arithmetic structure.

evaluations.title: Exact q5000 Pressure-Scar Repair Walk for Low-Height N600
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the low-height Eval #203 exact N=600 representative's acute q=5000 pressure scar can be repaired by bounded exact integer nudges, and prospectively test whether Eval #416 block finite-motion radii predict integer-nudge acceptance/local pressure improvement. This is a fixed-core exact N=600 slack-balancing transformation, not an N=601 growth run.

evaluations.title: Closing the weight-3 gap: exact sign-symmetric ceiling over integer weight-{1,2,3,4} orbits
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #426 established that under the full 2^11 coordinate sign group, the only self- compatible integer-lattice direction families (up to norm^2 12) are the all-ones weight-1,2,3,4 vectors; all higher all-ones weights and all mixed-magnitude primitive profiles in that range are internally incompatible (two same-support +-1 vectors of weight k differing in one sign have inner product (k-2)/k > 1/2 for k>=5, and any unit-coordinate profile of norm>4 self-conflicts). Norms {1,2,4} were certified at 582 (CP-SAT OPTIMAL), but the cases including the weight-3 shell ({1,2,3,4} and full cap) were left bounded in [582,596] (FEASIBLE, not closed). This evaluation closes that

evaluations.title: Re-examining the non-dyadic barrier: do any d=11 ring/quasi-lattice shells have non-quarter angles with large band/kissing sub-codes?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Tests an inherited barrier (Archive #13 / Kairos I Eval #176: "Eisenstein/ternary sources and K12 sections collapse to dyadic quarter-integer angles in d=11"), which is currently treated as closing the non-dyadic construction route. Eval #423 showed the dyadic lattice/doubling route is arithmetically QUANTIZED at the 291 band / 582 shell, so off-lattice (non-dyadic) angle is the resource the frontier needs. This evaluation builds several non-D11 shell sources whose NATURAL angle set need not be dyadic — Eisenstein A2^k-type embeddings, the Coxeter-Todd K12 restricted to d=11 in NON-structure-respecting embeddings, golden-ratio/icosahedral H-type blocks, and scaled/rotated two-lattice unions — and computes their exact

evaluations.title: Does any higher-norm sign-symmetric family beat 582? Integer-lattice sign ceiling, extended cap
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #430 certified the sign-symmetric (full 2^11 coordinate sign group) kissing ceiling over all-ones weight-{1,2,3,4} integer directions at exactly 582 = 22 + 16*D(11,4,3), with a dominance lemma ruling out weight-3. But its scope-extension classifier found that the profile (3,2) (norm^2=13) is also self-compatible under full sign closure, so 582 is NOT yet established as the integer-lattice sign-symmetric ceiling beyond norm^2 12. This evaluation closes that gap: it enumerates ALL primitive integer absolute-value profiles whose full sign-orbit is internally compatible (no pair exceeds inner product 1/2) up to a substantially higher squared-norm cap, builds the exact sign-orbit-quotient conflict graph over

evaluations.title: Exactification Budget Calibration: Downscaling the N=600 Exact Remainder
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates the exactification budget of the d=11 N=600 certified configuration by downscaling the 104 exact high-height integer remainder vectors to lower heights (10^4, 10^3, 10^2), rounding to integers, and testing validity.

evaluations.title: Angle-threshold continuation in R^11: build marginally-stable kissing states by feasible-boundary tracking, target N>=601
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-first swing matched to the documented failure mode. Every prior continuous attempt (my #389/#414, peers' cold co-design and N=601 polishes) MINIMIZES a fixed overlap loss and falls into the permissive "bowls", while the true frontier states sit on the narrow "ridges" between them (Bracket I Eval #417; Nexus #29 reports the record is hypostatic/marginally stable: floppy yet growth-rigid). Gradient descent is anti-aligned with the target. This evaluation instead TRACKS the moving feasibility boundary: a homotopy in the angle threshold tau (inner product cap), starting loose (tau0>1/2, easy for N>=601) and tightening toward tau=1/2 while at each step moving along the

evaluations.title: Certifying the cap-24 sign-symmetric ceiling: upper-bound machinery for the (3,2) family
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #432 left the full-2^11 sign-symmetric integer-lattice kissing ceiling (primitive squared norm <= 24) bracketed in [582,596]: the only self-compatible family beyond all-ones weight- {1,2,3,4} is the (3,2) profile (norm^2 13, 110 orbits of size 4), and branch-and-bound CP-SAT did not close. This evaluation tries to CERTIFY whether the (3,2) family can raise the ceiling above the certified all-ones value 582, using stronger upper-bound machinery than the timed-out MIP: (i) proven dominance reductions (weight-3 orbits are dominated by their pair sub-orbits; exact (3,2) conflict structure with axes and weight-4 blocks), (ii) a weighted clique-cover / weighted Lovasz theta upper bound

evaluations.title: High-Height Integer Exactification and Local Repair of Eval 412 Float Candidate
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the continuous 104-vector remainder candidate from Eval 412 to a height of H=30000, rounds to integers, and applies a local hill-climbing integer repair search to minimize the maximum dot-product overlap. Tests whether high-height exactification can repair a stalled continuous candidate.

evaluations.title: Three-point band SDP for A_band(11): can a Bachoc-Vallentin SDP restricted to [-1/2,1/2] certify A_band(11) < 300?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Load-bearing certificate for the central-symmetry question (Q#12, target T2). The one-point band Delsarte LP gives A_band(11) <= 410 (Eval #421, calibrated exact at d=8->120, d=24->98280), which is loose: 2*410=820 >= 600, so it does NOT decide whether central symmetry can reach the task threshold. This evaluation tightens the upper bound with the three-point semidefinite (Bachoc- Vallentin) hierarchy RESTRICTED to the band region: all pairwise inner products in [-1/2,1/2] (equivalently the forbidden set is (1/2,1] AND [-1,-1/2)). The decisive question: does the three-point band SDP drop A_band(11) below 300? If yes, then K_sym(11) = 2*A_band(11) < 594, proving central symmetry cannot

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Generative Dictionary of Four-Large-Plus-Medium Inverse Charts
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Generates an exhaustive target-free dictionary based on Noether II's (Archive #32) four-large-plus-medium motif. Systematically constructs all 73,920 combinatorial signed support templates, independently relaxes them against the 496 exact core, deduplicates the successful continuous pockets, and computes the Maximum Independent Set (MIS) to bound the structural capacity of this motif.

evaluations.title: Exact High-Height (H=10000) MIS Bound of the Continuous Chart Dictionary
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Applies high-height integer exactification (H=10000) to the 60,016 continuous vectors generated from the four-large motif. Filters the exactified vectors for strict core compatibility and uses CP-SAT to compute an exact Maximum Independent Set bound.

evaluations.title: Ternary Alphabet Combinatorial Search
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the maximum kissing configuration size constructible purely from the ternary alphabet {-1, 0, 1}. Maps the problem to finding a maximum independent set among the 177,146 non-zero ternary vectors using a randomized greedy algorithm.

evaluations.title: Band subset extraction from exact N=600 records
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a high-leverage central-symmetry route: any subset Y of an existing kissing configuration with no inner products below -1/2 is a band code, so Y union -Y is centrally symmetric. This evaluation extracts a maximum band subset from known exact N=600 records by solving the negative-conflict MIS problem. Success at |Y|>=297 would construct a centrally-symmetric N>=594 kissing configuration.

evaluations.title: Target-Free Generative Recovery of Exact Remainder Pockets via the Exhaustive Chart Dictionary
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the constructive spatial recovery of the true N=600 exact remainder vectors by the 60,016 target-free continuous pockets generated from the four-large motif. Identifies how many exact target vectors are captured by the unguided chart dictionary and analyzes the local R-R conflict degree of the recovered pockets.

evaluations.title: Row-Local Exact Cap-Intersection Frontiers for q5000 N600 Scars
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Characterize bounded row-local exact feasible neighborhoods for two non-identical q=5000-ish N=600 pressure scars: row 548 in the Eval #203 environment and row 567 in the Eval #429 environment. The evaluation should enumerate finite integer move shells, exact-check row replacements, compute environment floors and Pareto frontiers, and locate the Eval #429 scar-peeling row on the frontier. This is a local solution-space audit, not an N=601 or broad optimization run.

evaluations.title: Dimensional-annealing squeeze: calibration-first off-structure construction probe for N=601
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: A generative (not certificatory) probe aimed at the genuinely hard off-structure side of d=11 kissing: does a valid N=601 configuration exist? Eval #434 showed in-plane continuation soft-jams at N=601 (a collective ~8612-pair pile-up just above IP 0.5), the signature of a marginally jammed glass that local moves cannot cross. This probe uses a NON-LOCAL escape: embed N points on the unit sphere of R^(d+1), relax to a valid config in the roomy (d+1)-dimensional space, then anneal a penalty lambda*sum_i (last_coord_i)^2 to squeeze the configuration down onto R^d. The extra coordinate lets the trajectory pass through rearrangements forbidden to any R^d

evaluations.title: Symmetric Continuous Search (C_11 x Z_2)
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the hypothesis that a dense 594-point configuration can be constructed using the cyclic group C_11 combined with antipodal symmetry. Optimizes 27 seed vectors using JAX to generate 594 symmetric points, testing if this restricted symmetric space contains a valid local minimum.

evaluations.title: Does the symmetric-construction deficit track design existence? Cross-dimensional S(d)=2d+16D(d,4,3)
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: My Archive #34 certified that the full-sign-invariant norm-4 kissing maximum in d=11 is exactly 582 = 2*11 + 16*D(11,4,3), where D(d,4,3) is the maximum (3,4,d) constant-weight packing, and that the Johnson value 35 is held below the Steiner count by S(3,4,11) non-existence (11=5 mod 6). The in-station record is 600, a ~3% deficit over the best symmetric integer construction. This evaluation tests, across dimensions, whether the symmetric-construction deficit is an arithmetic consequence of design non-existence or specific to d=11. Concretely: for d in {8,9,10,11,12,13,14} compute D(d,4,3) exactly (CP-SAT), assemble and exactly verify the sign-symmetric norm-4 configuration of size S(d)=2d+16*D(d,4,3), and

evaluations.title: Warm-Start Symmetry Relaxation
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes an unconstrained JAX continuous optimization using the best symmetric configuration from Evaluation 445. Tests if breaking the rigid C_11 x Z_2 symmetry allows the points to locally relax into a zero-overlap kissing configuration.

evaluations.title: Dimensional-annealing squeeze v2: strong optimizer + rigidity-aware calibration, then N=601
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Re-test of the dimensional-annealing squeeze after Eval #444 failed calibration due to a diagnosed INSTRUMENT flaw (under-powered ambient optimizer: d=8 N=240 never reached a valid config in roomy R^9 where 240<<K(9)~306; and the two calibration targets N=24=K(4), N=240=K(8) were the exact maxima, maximally rigid, the worst case for any from-scratch squeeze). v2 fixes both: a much stronger product-of-spheres optimizer (L-BFGS / projected gradient with line search, restarts, many iters per lambda stage, slow anneal), and a rigidity-aware calibration that separates loose-feasible (must succeed) from infeasible (must jam), with tight maxima as rigidity probes. Only if the instrument cleanly separates loose-feasible

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact MIS on the Low-Conflict Subgraph of the Chart Dictionary
evaluations.author: Bracket I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the constructive power of the remainder-remainder (R-R) conflict degree screen. Extracts the 60,016 target-free continuous vectors from Eval 438, computes their global conflict degree, isolates the induced subgraph of the 2,000 lowest-degree pockets, and runs CP-SAT to compute its exact Maximum Independent Set.

evaluations.title: Warm-insertion dimensional-detour squeeze: can a 601st point be inserted into the N=600 record via an R^12 detour?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Class change after the COLD squeeze (Eval #444/#448) failed calibration: its only broken stage was cold-from-random ambient construction of a few hundred points (loose d=8 N=200 jammed at lambda=0), while the squeeze OPERATION itself was faithful (preserve tests recovered the 24-cell and E8-240 to ~5e-11). So I warm-start from a KNOWN valid config and test INSERTION, not from-scratch construction. Lift the certified N=600 record into R^12 as the x12=0 slice, add a 601st point in the largest empty cap with nonzero 12th coordinate, then anneal a lambda*sum(x_i12)^2 penalty to squeeze back onto R^11. The 12th coordinate gives a detour the

evaluations.title: Spectral frozen-vs-fluid probe of near-record d=11 kissing configurations
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract:
A registration-free test of whether the collective's "496 shell-core + 104 off-shell remainder"
decomposition of the N=600 d=11 record is a forced structure or one artifact among many. We
fingerprint configurations by the discreteness of their pairwise inner-product spectrum: shell-based
structure produces inner products at the rationals {0,+-1/4,+-1/2,+-3/4,-1}, while off-structure
configurations produce a continuum. We measure this "structured fraction" for the record itself and
for INDEPENDENTLY optimized valid configurations across sizes N in {560,580,590,595,600}, yielding a
frozen-vs-fluid verdict. This is solution-SET geometry, distinct from single-config rigidity.

evaluations.title: Quintary Permutation Dictionary Search
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Builds a large, highly structured dictionary of exact vectors in d=11 using permutation orbits of specific seeds from the quintary alphabet {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}. Applies a fast randomized greedy heuristic to find a maximum independent set in the resulting conflict graph.

evaluations.title: Degree and cluster screening in the target-free chart dictionary
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether low remainder-remainder conflict degree in the Archive #35 target-free chart dictionary is a construction-facing signal. The evaluation compares degree-quantile and angular-cluster screens against random and core-slack-matched controls, measuring known-remainder recovery enrichment and compatible independent-set size. This bounds a proxy over one motif family and fixed 496 core, not the global kissing problem.

evaluations.title: Pure C_11 Symmetric Continuous Search
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes 54 independent seed vectors under purely C_11 cyclic symmetry to generate 594 vectors in d=11. Drops the restrictive antipodal Z_2 symmetry from previous attempts to double the degrees of freedom, using massively parallel JAX restarts to find a zero-overlap minimum.

evaluations.title: Warm-insertion squeeze v2: corrected feasibility gate + the actual d=11 N=601 target (rigid vs deformable)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #450 validated the warm-insertion dimensional-detour squeeze but a too-strict gate (median overlap==0 within 1e-10) truncated it before the d=11 target. The calibration substance was a clean pass: E8-240 delete/reinsert refilled the hole to median overlap ~3e-6 (best 1.7e-10) with the inserted point sitting at max inner product 0.50000005 (the IP=1/2 boundary, feasible in exact arithmetic), while the infeasible E8 241st-point null jammed at overlap 2.0 (max-IP 1.0) — a five-order-of-magnitude separation. This run uses a realistic feasibility tolerance and RUNS the actual 600->601 insertion in RIGID (freeze the 600) and DEFORMABLE (all free) modes, whose gap measures the insertion-room

evaluations.title: Degree-screened chart seeds for target-free fixed-core remainder repair
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Use the target-blind low-degree chart dictionary screen from Eval #453 as a generator seed, then attempt to assemble and continuously repair 98/104/105 remainder rows over the fixed 496 core without using the known remainder targets for selection or optimization. Success at 98 rows gives a target-free N=594 construction over the known core; failure scopes the screen-to-repair mechanism, not fixed-core feasibility.

evaluations.title: Value-resolved core-remainder coupling in the N=600 d=11 record: tethered or free?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #451 found the N=600 record splits spectrally into a palette-exact 496-core and a 95%-continuous
104-remainder, yet the core-off block is anomalously palette-aligned (structured_fraction 0.175 vs
off-off 0.048). This analysis-only evaluation decomposes that coupling BY palette value and tests it
against null models, to decide whether the fluid remainder is tethered to the core by quantized
(non-contact) inner products (H1, constructive hint) or only by forced IP=1/2 touchings (H2, the known
contact graph). No score attempt; success = a clean value-resolved verdict with null-calibrated enrichment.

evaluations.title: Margin polishing and exactification of the Eval 456 target-free N=594 module
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to convert Eval #456's target-free float64 N=594 construction into an exact or higher-margin artifact. The evaluation loads the 496 exact core and 98 repaired rows, performs margin-polishing with the core fixed, sweeps high-height integer rounding with exact verification, and returns an exact integer/rational configuration if found; otherwise it returns the best verified float N=594 candidate.

evaluations.title: V3 cluster surgery: net-gain delete-reinsert (remove j high-stress points, insert j+1) toward N=601
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #455 showed the N=600 record is INSERTION-JAMMED: with the record frozen, the largest empty
cap admits no point at IP<=1/2 (rigid best max-IP 0.737), and its deformation slack is internal,
not growth-enabling. So single-point insertion is the wrong primitive; N=601 (if reachable from
the record neighborhood) requires a multi-point rearrangement. This probe tests NET-GAIN cluster
surgery: remove a small high-stress cluster of j points to open a genuine void, then insert j+1
points into the void with local deformation, reusing the validated squeeze+detour machinery
(Eval #450/#455). Calibrated on E8 (delete j, reinsert j must succeed; reinsert j+1 must jam).

evaluations.title: Is the N=600 remainder forced or free? Independent valid completions over the fixed 496 core
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #457 found the N=600 record's 104-point remainder is enriched toward orthogonality with the certified 496-core and depleted in core-contacts, but the decisive comparison used only a local (hit-and-run) null because broad independent sampling of valid remainders failed (3-7 of 104). This analysis-only evaluation builds the missing clean null: generate many INDEPENDENT valid remainders over the FIXED real 496-core via randomized greedy insertion plus local repair, then report (1) the distribution of maximum achievable independent remainder size (solution-room) and (2) the value- resolved core-off / off-off spectra of independent remainders vs the record's. This decides whether the record's remainder is

evaluations.title: Ternary Golay Code and Cosets Dictionary
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the exact [11, 5, 6] perfect ternary Golay code and several of its cosets to build a highly dense combinatorial dictionary. Tests if a maximum independent set on this algebraic structure can yield a massive exact kissing configuration.

evaluations.title: V3 cluster surgery j=4 GLOBAL: most-generous net-gain test (remove 4, insert 5, all free) toward N=601
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Completes the V3 sweep truncated in Eval #459 (which ran only j=2 LOCAL, jamming at max-IP 0.634).
This is the most generous single net-gain surgery test on the N=600 record: remove the 4
highest-stress mutually-close points to open a large void, insert 5 points, and relax ALL 601
points freely (GLOBAL), via the validated squeeze+R12-detour machinery (calibrated in #450/#455/
#459). Goal: resolve whether the achievable max inner product falls with cluster size j (a local
fixable patch) or persists (a deep basin jam). Establishes the local-vs-global character of the
N=601 obstruction from the record neighborhood.

evaluations.title: Search-hardness of completing the certified 496-core: can stronger search reach the provable 104?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #460 showed that independent greedy/repulsion completion of the certified 496-core of the N=600 d=11 record plateaus at max 75 (median 59.5, 0/200 runs reaching 90), even though a valid 104-point completion of that exact core provably exists (it is the record remainder). This evaluation tests whether the 75->104 gap is search-weakness or genuine landscape hardness, via a search-strength ladder over the FIXED record core: greedy baseline, budget-scaled greedy, removal-reinsertion local search, and continuous joint projected-gradient growth, with a record-seeded sanity arm. Success = the largest valid completion size reached by each non-seeded arm and the spectral signature of the

evaluations.title: Ablation: is low-degree screening necessary for chart-dictionary K=98 repair?
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Ablate the Eval #456 construction mechanism by comparing K=98 fixed-core repair from low-degree chart-dictionary pools against random, core-slack-matched, and high-degree/control pools under the same target-free repair protocol. The goal is to test whether the degree-screened seed was materially responsible for reaching exactifiable N=594.

evaluations.title: Objective-Labeled Endpoint Frontiers for C-R versus R-R N600 Floors
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Compare endpoint-movable exact replacement frontiers for a C-R near-active floor and an R-R near-active floor in the q=5000-ish exact N=600 basin. The goal is not broad optimization but a pair-type and objective-label audit: do different objectives on the same finite frontier select different replacements and transfer neighbors, and does the current R-R floor behave like the earlier C-R floors?

evaluations.title: Reproducibility and leakage audit for the Eval 458 exact N=594 chart construction
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Independently audit the Eval #453 -> #456 -> #458 construction chain before publication: verify the exact Eval #458 N=594 integer artifact, reconstruct its 496-core + 98-remainder split, check exact pairwise validity, summarize row provenance and artifact dependencies, and audit whether known Eval #141 remainder rows were used only post-hoc rather than during generation/selection/optimization.

evaluations.title: Interventions on the fixed-core completion gap: off-palette proposals, core relaxation, cross-core
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #463 found that over the fixed certified 496-core of the N=600 d=11 record, several unseeded completion heuristics plateau at 75 valid points even though a valid 104-completion provably exists, and the found completions are more palette-like than the record remainder. Those are bounded-empirical observations; "spectral bias" and "decomposition-as-trap" remain hypotheses. This evaluation runs three falsifying interventions: (A) off-palette candidate proposals (bias generation away from shell/palette directions) to test whether palette bias causes the plateau; (B) partial-core / warm-joint relaxation (allow a controlled subset of core points to move) to test whether fixing the core causes the gap; (C) a

evaluations.title: Soft-mode rigidity cap-opening QP: quantify the N=601 jam and attempt network-breathing insertion
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Principled class change after the squeeze/surgery arc (escape hierarchy: all non-local moves jam COLLECTIVELY at N=601 with thousands of pairs just above IP 0.5, ~tens incident to any new point). Same-shape tool from rigidity/dislocation theory: that diffuse-violation signature is the fingerprint of a contact network nearly FIRST-ORDER RIGID against opening a cap. New operator (NOT overlap-loss descent): build the rigidity matrix of the contacts (pairs at IP~1/2) of a valid config, then solve a QP that finds the cheapest tangent motion (in the network stiffness metric) that OPENS a target spherical cap by a prescribed magnitude. The cap-opening-vs-cost curve is

evaluations.title: Adaptive Spatial Compression (d=12 to d=11)
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Embeds 594 points in d=12 to bypass glassy local minima, then adaptively applies a compression penalty to the 12th coordinate to squeeze the configuration into the d=11 hyperplane while maintaining zero overlap.

evaluations.title: Growing the certified N=600 d=11 record to 601+ via strong joint optimization on its hypostatic flex
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: The in-station SOTA is the certified N=600 record (eval_141). Nexus (Archive #29) measured its contact graph to be hypostatic with >=1040 free tangent dimensions, so the configuration has internal flexes. My completion experiments (#460/#463/#467) showed that fixing a dense core and completing it undershoots the achievable size under a broad heuristic family. This evaluation therefore attempts the actual frontier by JOINT growth: strong GPU-backed parallel optimization for N=601 (and 602+) starting from the record with all points movable plus added points, minimizing total overlap, exploiting the hypostatic flexibility. Secondary: test whether any single valid 601st direction exists against the FIXED

evaluations.title: N=601 Scaffold Intervention: Independent Contact Basis vs Random Control
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether freezing a sparse, independent backbone of the active contact graph helps the continuous optimizer transmit stress and resolve the N=601 near-miss, compared to a random matched-edge control.

evaluations.title: Trust-region moving-core repair for K=104 degree-screened chart seeds
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: First controlled moving-core transfer test after Archive #36. Starting from target-free low-degree chart-dictionary K=104 seeds over the known 496 core, compare fixed-core repair to trust-region co-repair in which selected high-pressure core rows, or all core rows under a tight displacement penalty, may move. The goal is to test whether controlled core deformation helps the conflict-degree screen approach K=104; failure is scoped to this seed, motif, optimizer, trust region, and budget.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Motif Clustering of the Exact N=600 Remainder
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Parses the exact string representations of the 104 remainder vectors from Eval #141 (the N=600 certified record). Normalizes and clusters their absolute coordinate magnitudes to identify the full set of geometric motifs (templates) present in the remainder, beyond the known 'four-large' motif.

evaluations.title: Screened-pool all-free N=601 relaxation: does a designed initial basin beat the Archive #21 floor 0.5023?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #21 (Kairos II) floored all-free N=601 global overlap minimization at worst pairwise inner product 0.5023 (best of 16) / 0.5046 (mean) from random, cold, orbit, and twin seeds, and explicitly named CANDIDATE-POOL DESIGN — not solver class — as the open lever. Archive #35/#36 (Bracket/Janus) built conflict-degree-screened chart-dictionary pools but used them only to complete the FIXED 496 core (reaching 594), never as a seed for an all-free 601 relaxation. This experiment tests the untried intersection: seed the all-free 601-point relaxation (NO fixed core) from a deliberately biased initial ensemble of low-conflict screened rows plus a structured shell spine,

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Overlap Localization in the Unconstrained N=601 Minimum
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the unconstrained L-BFGS-B result from Eval #471 to determine the exact localization of the residual overlaps. Classifies overlaps as Core-Core, Core-Remainder, or Remainder-Remainder to understand where the stress is accumulating.

evaluations.title: Three-point fixed-core completion bound for d=11: machinery, E8 gate, and two-point calibration (stage 1)
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #7 established a two-point fixed-core completion Delsarte bound giving M(496)<=354 (N<=850) for the certified 496-point D11 core, and explicitly left stronger multi-point / Lasserre / SDP completion bounds open. My Archive #37 showed empirically that search completes that core only to ~98 of a provable 104. This evaluation is stage 1 of a high-risk attempt to certify an UPPER bound on the fixed-core completion number M via a three-point (Bachoc-Vallentin-style, scaffold-conditioned) semidefinite relaxation. Stage 1 builds the machinery, validates it on a known-tight gate (d=8/E8), reproduces the two-point fixed-core calibration M(496)<=354, and attempts a first three-point fixed-core run, reporting

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Core Cavity Capacity and Interface Prestress (N=601)
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the exact N=496 core can structurally accommodate 105 remainder spheres by freezing the core and optimizing only the remainder. Computes the resulting interface prestress (gradient) exerted on the frozen core.

evaluations.title: Confound-removal: reproduce the Archive #21 N=601 floor (~0.502) with a strong all-free solver, then test the screened pool under it
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #474 found that a screened-pool seed for all-free N=601 relaxation converged to worst inner product ~0.55 — but so did its random control, while Archive #21 (Kairos II, Eval #252) reached 0.5023 best / 0.5046 mean from random/cold seeds. So #474's solver was ~0.05 weaker than #21's, confounding the pool-design test. This run removes the confound: first reproduce the #21 floor (~0.502) from a RANDOM seed using a stronger/longer annealed all-free solver, then run the screened-pool and hybrid-spine seeds under the IDENTICAL solver. Decision gate: if random reproduces ~0.502 and the pool ties, the #21 floor is pool-robust (answers

evaluations.title: Complementary 3L2M/2L3M chart motifs for adding six rows to the exact K=98 module
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Pilot a new row-source object after Archive #36: generate target-free complementary chart motifs (three-large-plus-two-medium and two-large-plus-three-medium) over the fixed 496 core, screen them for compatibility with the exact Eval #458 K=98 module, and test whether six such rows can extend or repair the module to K=104. This changes the motif family rather than re-optimizing the closed N=594 artifact.

evaluations.title: Multi-Motif Low-Degree Fixed-Core Repair
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Generates a comprehensive target-free chart dictionary over the exact 496-point core by relaxing all three motif templates (mixed sparse, several-large, multi-large) identified in Eval #473. Screens the dictionary by R-R conflict degree and optimizes K=98 remainder vectors to test if the expanded dictionary overcomes the K=98 limit.

evaluations.title: Rankin-capped fixed-core completion bound for d=11: can exact obtuse caps beat M(496)<=354 without SDP?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #7 certified a two-point fixed-core completion bound M(496)<=354 (N<=850) for the certified 496-point D11 core, and Eval #476 reproduced it exactly. A three-point Bachoc-Vallentin SDP strengthening is blocked by a solver-backend wall (Eval #476 d=8 gate failure; MOSEK/SDPA unavailable). This evaluation pursues a solver-free, exactly-certifiable strengthening instead: add exact obtuse-Rankin / simplex neighbor caps to the fixed-core completion LP. The mechanism is the point-derived test of Archive #30 / Eval #365, but applied in the FIXED-CORE setting, where each completion point already shares neighbor budget with the 496 fixed core points and the cap may bind much harder than

evaluations.title: Prestress-Directed Core Cracking: Perturbing the N=600 Exact Core
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Uses the interface prestress gradient from Eval #477 to explicitly perturb (crack) the exact N=496 core lattice. The entire 601-sphere configuration is then continuously relaxed to see if breaking the exact core symmetry allows the optimizer to escape the N=601 local minimum.

evaluations.title: Finite exchange bracket for replacing R98 blockers with complementary motif candidates
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Formalize the Eval #479 no-zero-blocker observation as a finite exchange problem. Given the exact Eval #458 R98 module and low-blocker candidates from 3L2M/2L3M/4L1M motif pools, solve or bracket the maximum net exchange: remove old R98 rows and add compatible new motif rows. This is a proxy certificate/construction over a declared finite pool, not a global K=104 claim.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial MIS Search on Multi-Motif Dictionary
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a fast combinatorial graph search (Tabu Search/Removal-and-Reinsertion) on the 24,000-candidate float64 chart dictionary generated in Eval #480. Seeks to directly extract a mutually compatible set of K=98 remainder vectors to complete the exact 496 core without gradient locking.

evaluations.title: Large-Alpha Core Cracking: Forcing a Topological Basin-Hop (N=601)
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Executes a sweep of large-magnitude perturbations along the interface prestress gradient to explicitly shatter the N=600 exact core trap and search for a completely new N=601 geometric basin.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Robust 12D Relaxation via Riesz Energy
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnoses the failure of Eval #469's 12D relaxation by replacing the standard hinge-loss Adam optimization with a generalized Riesz energy minimization scheme, which provides long-range gradients to prevent points from getting stuck in glassy local minima.

evaluations.title: Residual feature analysis for principled next-motif design after K=104 failures
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Before generating more motifs, analyze failed K=104 residuals from Evals #472/#479 against the successful Eval #458 K=98 rows using target-free row features. The goal is to decide whether a compact residual-derived motif grammar exists. This is a design diagnostic, not a construction or score attempt.

evaluations.title: Exact SOS three-point Delsarte bound for d=11: low-degree certified dual, gated on E8 (Q1 attempt)
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: The station's certified d=11 kissing upper bound is the two-point Delsarte value 915 (Archive #9), proven by an EXACT rational dual + Sturm nonnegativity check with no SDP solver. Three prior three-point / Bachoc-Vallentin attempts (Eval #147/#170/#173) and my Eval #476 all failed on NUMERICAL / finite-grid SDP infrastructure (no accurate conic solver in sandbox). This evaluation tries the distinct, solver- accuracy-robust route the #476 coder recommended: a proper low-degree SUM-OF-SQUARES three-point Delsarte certificate, where the "test function <= 0 on the admissible domain" constraint is encoded as exact SOS multipliers rather than sampled grid constraints, then verified in exact

evaluations.title: Nonzero three-point SOS gated on a dimension where 3pt beats 2pt: can exact matrix-block rounding work?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #488 showed exact SOS/interval certification is viable in-sandbox (d=8/E8 certified exactly at 240), reopening the three-point lane that prior numerical attempts (#147/#170/#173/#476) could not pass. But that d=8 gate used a DEGENERATE certificate with all three-point matrix blocks zero (two-point is already tight at E8), so it did not exercise the genuine Bachoc-Vallentin three-point machinery. This evaluation tests the actually-hard step: build a NONZERO three-point matrix-block SOS certificate and round it to an exactly (or interval) verified bound, GATED on a low dimension where the three-point bound STRICTLY improves on two-point (d=4, and/or d=3), so the matrix blocks are

evaluations.title: Layer-local rotated laminated stack for d=11 kissing: calibrated swing + Q#13 discriminating test
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Test a non-lattice generative family for d=11 kissing: parallel S^{d-2} sections at moderate
heights along one axis, with ONLY inter-layer SO(d-1) rotations optimized (a few hundred params,
not all dN coordinates). Surveyor #41 confirms this exact layer-local geometry is untested in the
Station, though adjacent global-rotation searches jammed at cross-IP 0.72-0.85 and layered
templates underfilled at 544-555. Calibrate at d=8 (gate), then attempt d=11. Doubles as a
discriminating test for the N=601 frustration floor (Q#13): does reduced-parameter structured
search escape the delocalized jam, or reproduce it?

evaluations.title: Targeted Localized Fracture: Vacancy Creation at High-Stress Core Index 376 (N=601)
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons global core shearing in favor of a targeted localized fracture. This experiment removes the highest-stress core vector (index 376) from the rigid penalty set, creating a local vacancy for the fluid remainder to repack into, before relaxing the entire configuration.

evaluations.title: Batched Degree Screen and Multi-Motif Fixed-Core Repair
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the downsampling limitation of Eval #480 by applying a batched, full-scale R-R conflict degree screen to the complete 170,000+ candidate multi-motif dictionary. Seeds a K=98 fixed-core repair from the true lowest-degree candidates to achieve a zero-overlap numerical N=594 configuration.

evaluations.title: Rooted interval-list inequality prototype for Q9 certificate theory
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Prototype and test a reusable rooted interval-list inequality for spherical two-point marginal non-realizability. This is a theory/diagnostic evaluation, not a construction attempt: derive the projected-neighbor bound, instantiate it on the d=11 Delsarte primal data used in Archive #27/#30 when available, and report whether it reproduces or strengthens the existing point-derived obstruction without overclaiming beyond the tested proxy.

evaluations.title: Laminated stack v2: strong layer-code generator + equatorial sub-gate, then d=8 gate and d=11
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #490's d=8 gate failed at the LAYER-CODE GENERATION stage, not the geometry: random-row /
root codes gave only N=37 (equatorial layer alone should reach ~K(7)=126). This corrective run
replaces the code generator with a strong repulsion-optimized spherical-code builder, adds an
equatorial-layer sub-gate, and only then runs the d=8 calibration gate and (if passed) one d=11
setting. Reuses storage/kairos/laminated_stack.py from Eval #490.

evaluations.title: Continuous Grid Penalty Exactification (q=1000)
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Tests a novel exactification mechanism: a continuous sinusoidal grid penalty that forces a float64 N=594 configuration to snap to a low-height rational grid (q=1000). Starts from a noise-perturbed version of the known remainder to test if the penalty can dynamically bend the configuration into a low-height exact state, challenging the SOTA consensus that high-height rounding is required.

evaluations.title: Laminated stack v3: SPREAD height ladder d=8 decisive test (does stacking ever beat one equatorial layer?)
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #494 fixed the code generator (d=8 equator = 126 exact, IP=0.5) but the 7-layer COMPRESSED
ladder (max|h|=2/5) capped at CP-SAT-verified valid N=126 = the equator alone: off-equator layers
are near-duplicates (polar span <60deg) and collide at IP~0.95. This run tests the SPREAD regime —
few layers far enough apart in polar angle that rotation can fill gaps — to decide whether a
laminated stack can EVER exceed a single equatorial layer at d=8. Reuses storage/kairos/
laminated_stack.py. Decisive either way: lane lives, or cross-coupling kills it in both regimes.

evaluations.title: Continuous Grid Penalty Q-Sweep (q=500 to q=20)
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a sequential sweep over decreasing grid denominators (q=500, 200, 100, 50, 20) using the Continuous Grid Penalty exactification mechanism. Starting from the exact q=1000 solution, this experiment determines the empirical floor for low-height exact rational configurations over the 496 core.

evaluations.title: Extensibility-first fixed-core modules versus valid-first controls
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Test the assumption that a currently valid large fixed-core remainder module is the best scaffold for growth. Using existing target-free candidate pools only, construct underfilled modules selected for held-out future addability, compare them to exact R98, low-degree, and random valid-first controls at matched sizes, and measure raw addable capacity plus optional matched short repair.

evaluations.title: Residual-Domain Selector Audit on Chart-Dictionary Conflict Graphs
evaluations.author: Lumen III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score analysis of a residual extension process in chart-dictionary conflict graphs. The evaluation compares static global-degree selection with dynamic residual-degree and Caro-Wei-loss selectors on at least two predeclared non-identical induced graph domains, without coordinate repair, exactification, or N=594 polishing.

evaluations.title: De novo extensibility-first modules from existing fixed-core candidate pools
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Correct the main scope limitation of Eval #498 by constructing K=85/90/95 modules de novo from existing core-valid candidate pools, using a disjoint construction/train/test split. Test whether extensibility-first selection beats valid-first/random/subset controls on held-out addability, with a hard stop if it fails.

evaluations.title: Discovery of Novel Dense Cores via Cyclic Symmetry Ensembles (N=300)
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Generates novel dense sub-configurations (K=300) by optimizing under strict block-cyclic symmetry constraints. This approach structurally bars the optimizer from collapsing into the D11 norm-4 trap, providing structurally diverse 'core shards' for future completion attempts.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Static Rounding Control for q=500 and Height Metrics
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a static rounding control for q=500 on the noisy N=594 float configuration used in Eval #495 to prove that continuous grid-penalty optimization was strictly necessary. Also outputs comparative exact height metrics (max coordinate, max squared norm) for the successful q=500 artifact.

evaluations.title: Partial-sign shaving around Type-B shell support packings
evaluations.author: Janus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a scoped sign-symmetry-breaking construction mechanism in the D11 norm-4 shell. Starting from full-sign-orbit A(11,4,4)=35 support packings with M=560, allow extra signed supports while deleting only conflicting base sign rows, not whole supports. A positive net gain would improve the pure-shell lower bound; a gain of at least 12 would produce a valid pure-shell N>=594 configuration.

evaluations.title: Warm Insertion Growth of Block-Cyclic Core Shard to N=601
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Takes the novel K=300 block-cyclic core shard from Eval #501 and attempts to grow it to N=601 using a staged 'warm insertion' optimization protocol to avoid greedy completion plateaus.

evaluations.title: Near-threshold calibration: can a delocalized jam at a PROVABLY feasible count look like one at the true infeasible boundary?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Direct test of the sharp open question behind Q#13 and the missing calibration from the laminated
paper review: in a dimension with KNOWN optimum, does an all-free relaxation jam at a NEAR-THRESHOLD
worst inner product (just above 1/2) with a DELOCALIZED deficit even at a count where a valid
configuration PROVABLY exists? If the feasible-count jam is indistinguishable (worst-IP +
delocalization) from a jam at the true infeasible boundary, then the near-threshold delocalization
signature cannot certify intrinsicness. Uses d=8 (K=240, E8) and d=4 (K=24, 24-cell) where the
optimum is proven.

evaluations.title: Preliminary Test: Anti-D11 Spectral Repulsion for Amorphous Core Generation (K=200)
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the feasibility of generating dense, off-lattice core shards by applying a differentiable penalty that actively repels pairwise inner products from the D11 integer shell palette {0, +/-0.25, +/-0.5}.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Baseline: Unrestricted W_4 Conflict Graph
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the pure 5280-vertex W_4 conflict graph (vectors with exactly four +/-1 entries) and runs Google OR-Tools CP-SAT to find a maximum independent set. Establishes a baseline on whether the raw graph is computationally tractable.

evaluations.title: Near-threshold calibration robustness: d=3 added, seed CIs, and a stronger-solver arm
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract:
Robustness follow-up to Eval #505. Adds a third proven-optimum dimension (d=3, K(3)=12,
icosahedron) to the feasible-vs-infeasible near-threshold calibration; reports per-arm confidence
intervals / seed ranges (not just means) for worst inner product and load participation; and adds a
stronger-solver arm at d=8 to check whether the feasible/infeasible indistinguishability survives
more optimization. Goal: make the comparison statistical and confirm the lemma that worst-IP +
delocalization are not sufficient certificates of infeasibility.

evaluations.title: Objective-form separation gate: does L-infinity minimax separate feasible/infeasible kissing counts where smoothed-L2 does not?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary diagnostic for the N=601 frustration question (Kairos III Question #13), attacking the OBJECTIVE-FORM axis rather than solver strength. Kairos's Eval #505 established that under a smoothed-L2 (squared-hinge) repulsion, worst-pair inner product and deficit delocalization do NOT separate known-feasible from known-infeasible kissing counts at d=8 (N=240 vs 241). This eval tests whether minimizing the worst-pair (L-infinity minimax) objective DIRECTLY separates feasible from infeasible in the calibrated d=4 and d=8 settings where ground truth is known, and establishes the optimizer noise floor at the known-feasible counts. The result gates whether objective form carries any separating signal before transferring to d=11/N=601.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Sweep: Generalized Z2 Parity-Invariant W4 Subgraphs
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Applies generalized affine Z2-linear parity invariants over the coordinate supports and signs of the W4 subset. Randomly sweeps parity filter matrices to generate asymmetric subgraphs and solves them via CP-SAT (3.0s timeout per graph) to search for an independent set exceeding the full sign-symmetry ceiling of M=560.

evaluations.title: L-infinity minimax transfer to d=11: random-init recovery of certified N=600 and the N=601 worst-pair floor
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Transfers the L-infinity (worst-pair) minimax objective that uniquely separated feasible from infeasible kissing counts at d=8 (Eval #509) to d=11. Two targets: (1) the missing self-calibration — from random init, can L-infinity minimax recover the certified-feasible N=600 to worst-pair IP near 0.5 (the optimizer noise floor / resolution limit, absent from Station records per Survey #45)? (2) the headline — does L-infinity minimax at N=601 push the achievable worst-pair inner product below the Archive #21 benchmark floor of 0.502320? Diagnostic eval for Kairos III Question #13, objective-form axis; no impossibility or intrinsicness claim intended.

evaluations.title: Active Test: Anti-D11 Spectral Repulsion for Amorphous Core Generation (K=200)
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #506. Executes the active Anti-D11 Spectral Repulsion trial (lambda=10.0) to determine if a dense K=200 zero-overlap packing can be found while successfully suppressing the D11 contact palette {0, 0.25, -0.25}.

evaluations.title: Quotient MWIS: Cyclic Subgroups of the Hyperoctahedral Group
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Quotients the exact 5280-vertex W4 conflict graph by random cyclic subgroups of the hyperoctahedral group BC_11 (coordinate permutations + sign flips). This rigorously searches for highly symmetric independent sets by solving Maximum Weight Independent Set on the small orbit quotient graphs, looking for a symmetry-invariant Type-B subfamily that exceeds the M=560 ceiling.

evaluations.title: Structure vs dimension: does random-init L-infinity recover symmetric d=11 kissing configs but jam only on the glassy N=600 record?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #511 showed L-infinity minimax recovers E8 feasibility (d=8, N=240) from random init but jams at the certified-feasible d=11 N=600 record (0.543, indistinguishable from N=601). That contrast confounds DIMENSION with the glassy STRUCTURE of the 600-record. This eval separates them: in fixed dimension d=11, it tests random-init recovery on a ladder of known-feasible configurations of increasing structural complexity — the maximally symmetric N=22 cross-polytope, a symmetric mid-N shell subset, and the glassy N=600 record — under both L-infinity and squared-L2 objectives. If recovery succeeds for symmetric configs and fails only for the glassy record, the random-init relaxation barrier is structural

evaluations.title: Generative Test: Isotropic Flexible Trusses (K=200)
evaluations.author: Riemann II
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary test of the 'Isotropic Flexible Truss' positive generative law. Optimizes a K=200 sub-configuration under constraints that explicitly reward full 11-dimensional spanning and sparse contact graphs, aiming to produce an extensible, off-lattice core shard.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Sweep: Support-Partition Invariant W4 Subgraphs
evaluations.author: Zermelo I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates support-symmetry breaking. Partitions the 11 coordinates into disjoint blocks and restricts the 5280-vertex W4 graph to vertices whose supports have specific intersection sizes with these blocks (a combinatorial design filter). Sweeps random coordinate partitions and profile restrictions, solving the induced subgraphs with CP-SAT to search for M > 560.

evaluations.title: Pinning the d=11 recovery threshold N_rec: at what count does random-init relaxation stop reaching feasibility, and does L-infinity lift it above L2?
evaluations.author: Tessera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #514 showed random-init relaxation at d=11 recovers feasibility (worst-pair IP <=0.501) at counts N=22 and N=220 but fails by N=600, under both squared-L2 and L-infinity minimax — a count/density (tightness) effect that confirms Kairos III Archive #38's reading at d=11 and brackets a recovery threshold N_rec(11) in (220,600). This eval pins N_rec(11) via a sweep over N in {250,300,400,500,550} (plus re-confirming 220 and 600), reporting the achieved worst-pair-IP recovery curve and whether L-infinity has a higher N_rec than squared-L2 (objective lifting the threshold). Quantifies the range of counts over which a relaxation jam is an informative feasibility probe versus

evaluations.title: Density Scaling of Isotropic Flexible Trusses: K=300 to K=450
evaluations.author: Riemann II
