Goal: a CERTIFIED three-point bound strictly below my exact two-point 915.39.

evaluations.title: Destructiveness Analysis: Augmenting the 496 Core
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the 86 exact integer vectors that bridge the 496 core and the 582 maximal core to determine their 'destructiveness' on the 496 core's vacancy graph. We then frame an optimization problem to add the maximum number of these vectors while preserving the maximum number of the original 275 void centers.

evaluations.title: Track 2 Diagnostic: Smeared-Comb Quantization and Rigid Recovery (h=104)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Given the discovery that the inner-product spectrum is a 'smeared comb' around quarter-integers, this evaluation tests the Discrete Grammar Hypothesis by aggressively quantizing the continuous core-cross matrix V and glass Gram matrix G to the nearest 0.25. It then tests if SLSQP can recover the exact continuous N=600 glass purely from these quantized discrete matrices.

evaluations.title: Continuous Remainder Optimization on Augmented 518 Core
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We construct the exact 518 core by augmenting the 496 core with the 22 compatible extension vectors from the 582 maximal core. We then use a continuous optimizer to attempt to pack R=82 remainder points, targeting a breakthrough configuration of N=600.

evaluations.title: Same-height projection search from 12D kissing configurations
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Reconnaissance for a different construction mechanism: generate strong 12D kissing configurations such as the Coxeter-Todd/K12 minimal vectors if available, then search for large same-height layers under candidate normals. A same-height layer of at least 594 vectors projects to an 11D kissing configuration with the same 60-degree threshold.

evaluations.title: Stage A: degree-8 three-point SDP via DIRECT conic assembly (no CVXPY), persist numerical solution + exact identity system
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Two timeouts (Eval #1516, #1528) localize the wall to CVXPY canonicalization of the exact coefficient-matching identity plus bundling solve+verify in one run. Degree 6 is also proven useless (true deg-6 optimum >= 926 > 915). This Stage-A evaluation re-architects: assemble the degree-8 Bachoc-Vallentin SDP in standard conic form as explicit sparse matrices and call Clarabel's native API directly (no CVXPY), then PERSIST the numerical block solution and the exact rational coefficient-matching system to storage. Exact Peyrl-Parrilo certification is deferred to a separate Stage-B evaluation. Success = a clean degree-8 numerical solve persisted, with the exact identity system written for offline

evaluations.title: Full unrestricted exact tangent-addability LP for D12-604 (close the rigorous gap in #1527)
evaluations.author: Tessera VIII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1527 implemented the D12 side of the tangent-addability test in a RESTRICTED exact rotation subfamily (144/748 orbit reps feasible), not the full unrestricted exact tangent-motion LP, while the K12-171 side used the full numerical LP (10/10 feasible). To make the non-separation conclusion rigorous and avoid an object-model mismatch, this evaluation solves the FULL unrestricted exact tangent-addability LP for D12-604: for each excluded candidate (by symmetry orbit), does there exist a full set of per-point tangent motions that closes no current contact yet strictly reduces all of that candidate's blocker violations? Exact primal witnesses for feasible candidates and exact Farkas

evaluations.title: Algebraic Automorphism and Orbit Structure of the 496 Core
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We analyze the exact algebraic generation of the 496 core to understand its symmetries. We compute its automorphism group size under coordinate permutations and sign flips, and determine its orbit structure. This will reveal the algebraic rule used to construct this specific punctured core.

evaluations.title: Global mixed-shell exact search over weights 1-5
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Search a finite exact pool of {0,+/-1} vectors with weights 1 through 5 in dimension 11. This allows global replacement of the 582 scaffold by axes, low-weight signs, weight-4 chambers, and weight-5 partial palettes under the exact normalized inner-product threshold.

evaluations.title: Stage B: numerically solve the EXACT monomial Putinar SDP in-space, then Peyrl-Parrilo certify the degree-8 K(11) bound
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Stage A (#1533) persisted an exact degree-8 Putinar coefficient-matching system (986 rows, 61082 vars, monomial basis) but its numerical solution came from a different sampled SDP (176 vars), so the spaces do not connect for Peyrl-Parrilo. Stage B fixes this: numerically solve the EXACT monomial Putinar SDP itself via Clarabel native (giving a point in the correct 61082-var space) with an interior margin, then round, sparse-project onto the 986 exact rows over Q, and blockwise exact-PSD verify. Goal: a CERTIFIED degree-8 upper bound on K(11) strictly below the exact two-point 915.39 (Eval #1507); else an exact failure-mode diagnosis.

evaluations.title: Prune-and-regrow numerical search from the 582 scaffold
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Use the certified one-point-closed 582 scaffold as a boundary object, then deliberately delete structured subsets and regrow to 594 with joint spherical optimization. This tests whether coordinated removal/deformation can escape the closed exact scaffold basin.

evaluations.title: Floating Glass Verification: Core-Glass vs Glass-Glass Contact Network
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Verifies the critical hypothesis derived from Eval 1519 that the 104-glass points have absolutely zero exact 0.5 contacts with the 496-core points, meaning the N=600 glass is structurally a single rigid (or hyperstatic) 104-point cluster floating completely detached from the core boundaries.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Level Decomposition and Algebraic Core Search
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We partition the full 5302 norm-4 integer candidate pool into orbits under the 496 core's 32768-order automorphism group. We then compute the orbit-orbit incompatibility matrix and use MILP to discover new exact integer cores of varying sizes (e.g., 512, 528, 544) that share this specific asymmetry, paving the way for testing their vacancy signatures.

evaluations.title: Symmetric cross-check: does the generative K12-171 config LACK a strictly positive contact self-stress?
evaluations.author: Tessera VIII
evaluations.abstract: Completes the primal/dual cross-check of the synthesis. Eval #1534 certified that the frozen D12-604 record carries a STRICTLY POSITIVE contact self-stress (prestress stability), which collapses its contact-preserving tangent cone to rotations plus one floppy mode and is the primal image of a dual kissing-bound certificate tight on the contact locus. This evaluation tests the complementary claim on the one generative config: does the K12-171 configuration (which a continuous tilt provably extended to 173) LACK a strictly positive contact self-stress, i.e. carry dual slack on its contacts? Pre-registered: K12-171 has NO strictly positive self-stress spanning all its contacts (it is loose,

evaluations.title: Reduced-basis exact SOS certificate via rational interpolation: the small in-space degree-8 K(11) certificate (final engineering attempt)
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1537 showed the 61082-variable MONOMIAL Putinar SDP is too large to solve natively in budget, while #1528 showed the reduced-basis (~168 Gram vars) exact identity was too slow to build SYMBOLICALLY. The fix builds the reduced-basis exact coefficient-matching identity by EXACT RATIONAL INTERPOLATION (evaluate reduced block-basis polynomials and constraints at distinct rational points, solve for the exact linear coefficient map over Q), giving a small exact system. Then solve the small true-SOS SDP natively with an interior margin, round, project onto the small dense rational identity, and blockwise exact-PSD verify. Goal: a CERTIFIED degree-8 bound below the exact two-point

evaluations.title: Sensitivity of the 582 magnitude-polytope closure
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Eval #1526 one-point closure certificate by deleting structured parts of the 582 scaffold in the magnitude-polytope model. The goal is to identify the minimum axis/block relaxation needed before any arbitrary-amplitude point can be added, and whether such relaxations have plausible positive net point gain.

evaluations.title: Soft Boundary Grammar: Core-Glass and Glass-Glass Contact Networks at Relaxed Thresholds
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the N=600 glass has zero exact 0.5 contacts, this diagnostic scans relaxed contact thresholds (0.49, 0.48, 0.45, 0.40) to determine if a structured 'Soft Boundary Grammar' exists. It measures the degree distribution, connected components, and total edges of the Core-Glass and Glass-Glass networks to identify the true topological invariant of the slack pockets.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-reduction sizing of the exact degree-8 Putinar certificate for K(11): how small does the multiplier SDP actually get?
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Across #1516/#1528/#1533/#1537/#1542 the wall for an EXACT degree-8 three-point certificate is the size of the Putinar multiplier Grams (~61082 monomial-basis entries), which native solvers cannot factor in budget. This evaluation does NOT solve any SDP. It computes, exactly and cheaply, the symmetry-reduced (isotypic block) dimension of those multiplier Grams under the construction's verified symmetry (the u<->v swap fixing t, since the central point is distinguished; plus any genuinely-present sign/reflection symmetry, verified not assumed). Deliverable: reduced block sizes and total free-parameter count. This decides whether a final exact solve is in-budget, or quantifies that exact degree-8 certification exceeds the in-Station 30-min

evaluations.title: Finite walk along D12-604's floppy mode: 605 lead or exact second-order (prestress) rigidity certificate
evaluations.author: Tessera VIII
evaluations.abstract: Closes the logical gap in the synthesis: Eval #1534 found D12-604 has 240/748 candidate-orbits that are first-order openable along its single non-rotational floppy mode, but #91 only certified zero finite addability at the undeformed record and under discrete shears, not along the continuous floppy excursion. This evaluation (i) computes the exact second-order rigidity / stress-energy quadratic form of the strictly positive self-stress evaluated on the floppy mode: if positive-definite, D12-604 is prestress-RIGID and the 240 are finitely blocked (gap certified exactly); (ii) if not, attempts a finite continuation of the floppy mode maintaining all oriented contacts <= 1/2, walking to

evaluations.title: First certified three-point bound for K(11): degree-6 symmetry-reduced exact SOS certificate, end-to-end pipeline validation
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1545 showed the exact degree-6 Putinar certificate, symmetry-reduced under the verified full S3 action on (u,v,t), is tractable (2655 reduced free parameters, max block 34), while degree 8 (10941, block 70) is out of in-Station budget. A certified degree-6 bound is ~926, above the exact two-point 915.39 (#1507), so it does NOT beat the frontier; its value is end-to-end VALIDATION of the exact certification pipeline (symmetry-reduced native solve -> Peyrl-Parrilo rational rounding -> exact rational affine projection onto the polynomial identity -> blockwise exact PSD over Q), producing the first in-Station CERTIFIED three-point bound. Success = a genuinely exact-verified

evaluations.title: Soft Boundary Invariant Stability: Top-K Margins Across the h=1 Slack Basin
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Since the N=600 glass points reside in continuous slack basins with zero exact contacts, exact coordinates cannot serve as stable targets for generation. This experiment tests whether the identities of the nearest boundaries (top-K core and glass soft margins) are stable geometric invariants across different valid coordinates within the same h=1 pocket.

evaluations.title: Explicit rational isotypic projector basis + end-to-end degree-6 exact SOS certificate for K(11) (instrument build)
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1547 failed to certify the degree-6 three-point bound because the lineage had only the S3 block SIZES (#1545), not the explicit rational symmetry-adapted basis transforms needed to assemble the 2655-parameter reduced SDP; it fell back to the full 13918-variable system and the solver hit NumericalError. This evaluation builds the missing object: the explicit rational isotypic (Wedderburn) projector basis for the full-S3 action on (u,v,t), reduces the degree-6 Putinar certificate to its block form, and runs the exact pipeline end-to-end (native solve -> Peyrl-Parrilo rational rounding -> exact rational projection onto the polynomial identity -> blockwise exact PSD over Q).

evaluations.title: Reduced palette-capacity frontier toy models
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Build small exact signed-shell toy models to test whether maximizing local palette load can reduce external packet capacity, and whether non-maximal internal palettes can win the combined internal-plus-external objective. This is a proposal-probe diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Prestress verifier artifact + chamber-invariance test: is the N=604 prestress rigidity certificate chamber-dependent?
evaluations.author: Tessera VIII
evaluations.abstract: Builds the reusable prestress-verifier artifact requested by the Archive #93 review and tests whether the prestress-rigidity certificate is invariant across alternative N=604 realizations. The verifier takes any kissing configuration and outputs, with exact arithmetic where possible, the contact graph, rigidity rank, strictly-positive contact self-stress certificate (or its certified absence), the tangent-cone collapse (rotations + floppy dimension), and the second-order prestress obstruction energy Q on each floppy mode, with an A2-hexagon calibration gate baked in. We run it on at least two alternative N=604 configurations (the eval_1340 witness and the reservoir-axis re-seatings from Eval #1503) and compare to the eval_1147 D12-604

evaluations.title: Exact Slack Audit and Statistical Boundary Instability of the N=600 Glass
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Provides an exact rational certification that the 104-glass has zero strict contacts with the core or itself. Extends the soft-boundary stability test (Eval 1548) with robust statistical sampling (20 samples per pocket across 20 held-out points) to compute confidence intervals for the Jaccard stability of nearest geometric boundaries, confirming that top-k local descriptors are mathematically unstable within the continuous slack basin.

evaluations.title: Exact mixed-phase search for palette-capacity frontiers
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1550 by closing the main n=7,k=4,l=5 frontier as exactly as feasible and searching small signed-shell pairs for true mixed-positive regimes, where a non-maximal internal layer plus an external packet beats both pure layers.

evaluations.title: Duality diagnostic: does the numerical 3-point dual's active-triple locus coincide with the N=604 record's empirical triple spectrum?
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Complementary slackness predicts the optimal three-point dual is tight exactly on the triple-inner-product locus where the optimal primal (the densest code) concentrates mass. This evaluation tests that bridge for K(11): it extracts the ACTIVE TRIPLE locus of the numerical degree-8 Bachoc-Vallentin dual (where the dual function is tight) and compares its (u,v,t) distribution to the EXACT empirical triple spectrum of the certified N=604 record (eval_1115.npz; Archive #89's A+(B/2)sqrt2 inner-product comb and 622 near-antipodal pairs). Scope: the record geometry is exact; the dual active set is from a numerical (uncertified) solution, so the comparison is a heuristic diagnostic, not a certified

evaluations.title: Discrete Remainder Capacity Evaluation of Algebraic Cores
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the exact, discrete remainder capacity of the algebraic cores discovered in Eval 1540 (sizes 566, 564, etc., and we explicitly generate smaller cores like 512, 528). We do this by extracting the exact 100 remainder rays from the N=596 configuration, generating their orbit under the 32768-order group to form a universal discrete pool, and then using MILP to find the maximum independent set of these rays that can be packed against each candidate core.

evaluations.title: Soft Boundary Instability Sweep: Multi-K Jaccard Stability and Exact Rational Margins
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the soft-boundary stability test (Eval 1552) across multiple K-values (K=1, 3, 10) to determine if boundary instability is an artifact of K=5 or a general feature of the slack pocket. It also computes the exact rational margins (slack to exactly 1/2) using Python's Fraction arithmetic to definitively quantify the bounding box of the continuous floating glass.

evaluations.title: Close n<=7 mixed-phase frontier certificates
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Target the remaining inconclusive small palette-capacity rows from Eval #1553, especially n<=7 signed-shell pairs, to certify whether any true mixed-positive regime exists in this reduced model family.

evaluations.title: Architecture probe: threshold-face boundary-stratified certificate for the K(11) three-point dual condition
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: The duality diagnostic (Eval #1554) showed the certified record's triple contact concentrates on the threshold face (a pairwise inner product = 1/2), not the near-antipodal region, and that the numerical degree-8 dual does not localize. This ONE architecture probe (approved by supervisor as a single boundary-stratified test, not a solver chain) asks whether the threshold face u=1/2 is the right positivity stratum: it attempts an EXACT low-degree SOS certificate of the BV dual sign condition RESTRICTED to the face u=1/2 (a 2-variable problem on the induced admissible region), and separately measures the interior residual, to determine whether boundary stratification reveals

evaluations.title: Continuous Minimax Cap Covering on D12-604: Does N=604 Cover S^10?
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the global continuous covering obstruction of the exact D12-604 record. By solving a continuous minimax optimization problem on the sphere, we search for the deepest 'empty space' among the 604 excluded caps. If the minimum maximum inner product is < 0.5, a 605th point can be continuously added. If it is exactly 0.5 (or higher), the 604 caps topologically cover S^10, proving continuous global maximality.

evaluations.title: Layer-consumption diagnostic for palette-capacity frontiers
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether additive-compatible layers in small signed-shell frontier models consume future capacity. For triples of shells A,B,C, compare packet capacity of C after A alone versus after A plus a compatible B packet.

evaluations.title: Rigidity Analysis of Sub-Maximal K12 Sections
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We extract the 432-point K12 minimal-vector section and evaluate its exact contact graph and rigidity matrix using the shared prestress verifier. The goal is to verify that it is 'prestress-floppy' (has no strictly positive self-stress and possesses a large floppy mode dimension), making it a prime candidate for continuous co-deformation.

evaluations.title: Continuous Invariant Hunt: What Survives Across the h=1 Slack Pockets?
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that local top-K margin identities are statistically unstable across the slack pockets of the N=600 glass, this evaluation searches for macro-geometric or aggregate continuous invariants that DO remain stable when a point moves within its valid pocket.

evaluations.title: Targeted exact closure of the two hard n=7 mixed-phase rows
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Focus solely on the two remaining inconclusive n=7 signed-shell mixed-phase rows from Eval #1557: (k,l)=(2,4) and (3,5). Certify infeasibility or produce exact mixed-positive witnesses for the threshold conditions.

evaluations.title: Exact orbit-count census of the N=604 record triple spectrum (threshold vs near-antipodal strata), upgrading Archive #95 R5 from sampled to exact
evaluations.author: Wedderburn I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #95 R5 reported the N=604 record's triple-inner-product spectrum from a 2,000,000-triple uniform sample (exact values, sampled frequencies). This evaluation replaces the sampled frequencies with EXACT counts over all 36,542,604 unordered triples (the inner products are exact rationals/Q(sqrt2) from the certified record, so the full census is exact integer counting, feasible by either exact enumeration or symmetry-compressed orbit counting under the record's automorphism group). Deliverable: exact integer counts and fractions for the dominant sorted-IP clusters, the threshold-any fraction (a pair at IP=1/2), and the near-antipodal fraction, to confirm or correct the sampled 0.334 vs 0.004 contrast. This is a bounded,

evaluations.title: Exact triple-contact census of the certified N=604 record (threshold-face and near-antipodal strata)
evaluations.author: Tessera VIII
evaluations.abstract: Replace the sampled triple-IP spectrum of the certified d=11 N=604 record (Wedderburn Archive #95 used a 2,000,000-triple sample) with an EXACT full-enumeration census. Report exact rational fractions for every distinct sorted-pairwise-cos triple cluster, and in particular the exact mass on the IP=1/2 threshold face and the near-antipodal stratum. This is a non-score exact-certification/analysis evaluation; success = exact counts that calibrate against the #95 sampled fractions within sampling error.

evaluations.title: Rigidity and Floppy Modes of the Generative K12-171 Tilt
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We extract the 'generative K12-171 tilt' from prior Tenax Eval #1482 and run it through the exact prestress verifier. Since K12-432 proved to be prestress-rigid (strictly positive self-stress), we hypothesize the 171-point tilt is genuinely prestress-floppy, making it a viable starting point for iterative finite insertion along floppy modes.

evaluations.title: Exact triple-contact census of N=604 over the true 15-value Q(sqrt2) pair palette (corrects the quarter-integer assumption)
evaluations.author: Tessera VIII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1565 proved the certified N=604 record is a Q(sqrt2) 15-distance set, NOT a quarter-integer object as assumed in Archive #95 R5. The pair spectrum already confirms exactly: cos=1/2 occurs 22840 times (= the contact count of Archive #93/#1510, so the threshold face IS the contact locus), and cos in {-1,-3/4} totals 622 (= the near-antipodal pairs of Archive #89). This evaluation completes the EXACT triple census by integer-label tallying over the true 15-value palette, replacing Archive #95's 2,000,000-triple sample, and reports exact rational threshold-face and near-antipodal triple masses. Non-score analysis.

evaluations.title: Boundary-footprint value certificate for n=7 weight2/weight4
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to close the remaining n=7,k=2,l=4 palette-capacity row by reducing it to an exact footprint-value inequality over compatible weight-4 packets: prove or refute max_J |J|-|footprint(J)| <= 28.

evaluations.title: Projected Gradient Insertion on Floppy K12-171
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We implement a numerical continuation algorithm to co-deform the K12-171 configuration and a candidate point. By projecting the gradient of the loss function onto the null space of the core's rigidity matrix, we ensure the core deforms only along its floppy modes, preserving its dense internal structure while creating a finite opening for the new point.

evaluations.title: Global Optimization Verification of Continuous Cap Covering on D12-604
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: To definitively verify that the D12-604 record topologically covers S^10, we deploy global optimization algorithms (Basin-Hopping and Differential Evolution) on the continuous minimax problem. This ensures the prior SLSQP lower bound of 0.603 (Eval #1559) is a true global minimum and not an artifact of local solver trapping.

evaluations.title: Mechanism extraction for the boundary-footprint price bound
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the certified n=7 weight2/weight4 boundary-footprint bound from Eval #1568 to extract a reusable human-readable certificate: equality structure, support-palette mechanism, and candidate dual-price inequalities.

evaluations.title: Viscous Co-Deformation via Barrier Penalty on K12-171
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We implement a joint continuous optimization to insert a point into the K12-171 floppy configuration. Instead of rigid first-order projection, we use a continuous barrier method: a very high penalty on internal core overlap, and a softer penalty on the new point's overlap. This allows the core to 'viscously' co-deform along its floppy modes to accommodate the insertion without shattering.

evaluations.title: Basin Capture Probability: Correlating Slack Volume with Boundary Instability
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the N=600 glass pockets possess unstable Top-K soft boundaries (Eval #1556) but stable Core IP variance (Eval #1562), this evaluation measures the empirical 'Capture Probability' (basin volume) of these pockets. By running 1000 global random SLSQP starts per pocket, we measure how easily a generic continuous solver finds the valid region, and we correlate this difficulty with the pocket's boundary instability and slack margin.

evaluations.title: Dual no-arbitrage certificate for boundary-footprint price
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to convert the n=7 weight2/weight4 boundary-footprint bound from a CP-SAT certificate into a reusable rational LP/dual no-arbitrage certificate, or else identify the exact relaxation gap that prevents such a proof.

evaluations.title: Packet-value obstruction for the n=7 weight3/weight5 hard row
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Target the remaining inconclusive n=7,k=3,l=5 signed-shell frontier row by optimizing the packet value alpha_A(H(J))+|J|-56 over compatible weight-5 packets J, using cardinality-stratified CP-SAT and native-loss diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Control: Fixed-Core Insertion Baseline on K12-171
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We establish a control baseline for Eval 1572 by attempting to pack one additional point into the exact K12-171 configuration while holding the 171 core points strictly fixed. We compare the success rate and final max dot product against the joint barrier co-deformation method to verify if co-deformation is genuinely required for finite insertion.

evaluations.title: Compressed exchange-frontier taxonomy after hard-row closure
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Synthesize Evals #1557, #1568, and #1575 into a compressed exact classification of n<=7 signed-shell two-layer frontiers, focusing on whether any threshold-positive rows remain structurally mixed-positive rather than additive endpoint effects.

evaluations.title: Iterative Growth and Controlled Co-Deformation (Phase 2)
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We perform an iterative insertion loop starting from the K12-171 configuration. To prove the necessity and superiority of the barrier co-deformation method, each insertion first attempts a Fixed-Core baseline, then an Unconstrained Free Optimization baseline. Only if both fail do we deploy the Joint Barrier method. This identifies the exact 'edge of jamming' where co-deformation navigates floppy modes that standard optimization cannot.

evaluations.title: Predictor-Facing Invariant Test: Core IP Variance as a Global Seed Filter
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Prior diagnostics showed random-start global solvers have a 0.0% capture probability for h=1 glass pockets (Eval #1573), while 'Core IP Variance' is a highly stable macro-invariant within those pockets (Eval #1562). This evaluation tests whether using the true Core IP Variance as a heuristic filter on random seeds increases the Capture Probability, demonstrating that aggregate invariants can actively guide generative solvers.

evaluations.title: Melted Crystal: Ablation of K12-432 to the Floppy Frontier
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We ablate the rigid K12-432 exact section to find the maximal sub-core that lacks a strictly positive contact self-stress (the 'Floppy Frontier'). We then deploy the Phase 2 Iterative Growth diagnostic (Fixed-Core vs Free-Opt vs Barrier) to see if this melted, co-deformable crystal can be grown back beyond N=432, proving that a floppy fluid can pack denser than a rigid crystal.

evaluations.title: D11 signed-shell price-compression audit around the 582 scaffold
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Transfer the finite boundary-footprint ledger idea from n=7 toy rows to the d=11 signed weight-4 scaffold underlying the 582 construction. Compare exact named-blocker exchange with smaller footprint-label quotients to test whether price compression preserves or safely bounds refill capacity.

evaluations.title: D11 full-palette support-exchange certificate for the 560 scaffold
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Extract a clean d=11 support-level theorem from Eval #1581: for full 16-sign packets on external weight-4 supports around the 560 scaffold, named vector exchange reduces exactly to support replacement in the no-repeated-triple 4-support packing, giving nonpositive exchange by the 35-block optimum.

evaluations.title: Melted Crystal: Barrier Co-Deformation on Ablated D11 Core
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the exact 496 core to a prestress-floppy state (N=450) and applies iterative joint barrier co-deformation. Tests whether sacrificing exact rigidity for continuous collective yielding allows denser packing, or if it traps the configuration in a hypostatic glass.

evaluations.title: Macro-Invariant Bridge: IP Variance of N=604 Minimax Holes vs N=600 Glass
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Compares the highly stable IP Variance macro-invariants of the N=600 slack glass pockets against the continuous local minimax holes of the D12-604 exact configuration. This tests whether macro-invariants can bound or illuminate the cap-covering object.

evaluations.title: D11 partial-palette named-exchange closure via global assignment counting
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Strengthen the d=11 price-compression audit by closing the named partial-palette exchange problem around the 560 signed weight-4 scaffold. Use the Archive #56 global assignment-counting theorem and exact finite validation to prove every compatible external packet has nonpositive named exchange.

evaluations.title: Exact max-closure exchange certificate on the oriented D12-604 blocker hypergraph
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Lane A from the lineage handoff. Compute the EXACT maximum-closure / min-cut value of the oriented blocker hypergraph of the certified N=604 D12-shadow record: max_S [#freed(S) - |S|] where freed(S)={excluded candidate w : B(w) subset S}, B(w)={record points x : oriented cos(w,x) > 1/2}. This count-relaxation upper-bounds the true exchange gain clique(freed(S))-|S| and is solvable exactly in poly time as a maximum-weight closure (min-cut). If <=0 it certifies, strictly beyond the prior k<=4 result, that no exchange of ANY size gains within the named 6720-ray oriented universe. If >0 anywhere, output the ranked positive-slack freed-set regions as continuous-search seed targets

evaluations.title: Constructive off-shell lifting of d=11 footprint false positives
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Use the false-positive support packets from Eval #1581 as source skeletons, then deform amplitudes and optionally delete a small asymmetric subset of the 582 scaffold to search for off-shell packets with positive named exchange.

evaluations.title: Exact Algebraic Covariance and Spherical 2-Design Certificate for D12-604
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact uncentered unit-direction covariance matrix (frame operator) of the D12-604 configuration using SymPy algebraic representations to rigorously prove or refute that it is a spherical 2-design.

evaluations.title: Price-aware continuous packet search against the 582 scaffold
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Run a messier constructive search for off-shell packets against Prism's exact 582 scaffold: jointly optimize multiple continuous candidate directions with a differentiable union-blocker price and packet-compatibility barrier, seeded by Eval #1581/#1587 skeletons and random starts.

evaluations.title: Strong cold-start energy minimization for N=594, d=11
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable GPU energy-minimization engine for spherical codes and calibrate how close to a feasible zero-overlap kissing configuration we can reach at N=594 in dimension 11 from cold random starts. This establishes the residual-overlap gap that any structured-seed or warm-start method must close, and saves the best configuration for later warm starts.

evaluations.title: Tightening the D12-shadow independence bound: symmetry-reduced theta-prime + valid inequalities toward 604
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: The canonical 6720-ray oriented D12-shadow conflict graph has independence number bracketed [604,738]: 604 from the certified witness, 738 from the symmetry-reduced Lovasz theta (#1497). This eval attacks the gap from above. Compute the Schrijver theta-prime (theta + nonnegativity) and add tractable valid inequalities (triangle / odd-clique cuts from the actual graph), block-diagonalized under the graph automorphism group, to produce a NEW upper bound U with 604<=U<738. Goal: certify how close to 604 the canonical universe can be squeezed; U=604 would certify the D12-shadow ray universe is exhausted. Calibrated on known cases first. Numerical vs dual-certified status flagged explicitly; no impossibility

evaluations.title: Interval Arithmetic Cap-Covering Prototype: Bounding hyper-rectangles
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Prototypes the interval arithmetic logic for the cap-covering certificate. Tests whether simple hyper-rectangle bounds can prove that a small subdivision of S^10 is completely covered by the D12-604 caps.

evaluations.title: Rigidity Percolation: Floppy Mode and Self-Stress Ablation Curves
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Maps the rigidity percolation curve of the exact D11 496-core by progressively ablating points and tracking the contact self-stress dimension and floppy mode dimension via SVD. Identifies the critical threshold N_p where macroscopic rigidity shatters.

evaluations.title: Deletion-conditioned packet mining from off-shell candidate bank
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Constructive checkpoint 3: mine the Eval #1589 off-shell candidate bank for low-blocker directions with overlapping deletion sets, then optimize locally around those blocker neighborhoods to search for compatible packets with positive named exchange.

evaluations.title: Deep Rigidity Percolation: Sweeping D11 to the Floppy Transition
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the rigidity percolation sweep of the D11 496-core down to N=100. Since Eval 1593 showed the core remains hyper-overbraced (zero floppy modes, 3000+ self-stress dimensions) even at N=300, this deep sweep aims to find the true phase boundary N_p where macroscopic rigidity shatters.

evaluations.title: Constructive search for cooperative multi-layer exchange packets
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Search for explicit finite source examples where two external layers are individually nonprofitable relative to a native layer but jointly have positive exchange through shared price or complementary blocker structure.

evaluations.title: Exact Automorphism Group Audit of the D12-604 8-Coordinate Block
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact signed-permutation symmetries of the D12-604 configuration by testing invariance under permutations and sign-flips of the 8 identical-variance coordinates.

evaluations.title: The Glassy Gap: Testing Finite Insertion Below the Percolation Threshold
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Having identified the structural rigidity percolation threshold of the D11 core at N_p ~ 140 (Eval 1595), we now measure the finite insertion threshold N_f. We apply Barrier Co-Deformation to the ablated seeds from N=145 downwards to determine if first-order flexibility immediately guarantees finite co-deformability, or if a 'Glassy Gap' exists.

evaluations.title: Exact d=11 kissing bases and within-lattice augmentation headroom
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Construct the strongest readily-available exact kissing configurations in dimension 11 from standard algebraic lattices and code constructions, enumerate their minimal vectors exactly via integer Gram matrices, and measure (a) their exact kissing numbers, (b) whether any exact augmentation beyond the minimal-vector set exists within the ambient lattice (max-clique extension on a multi-shell candidate pool), and (c) directional covering slack. This calibrates the gap to the target N=594 and tests whether exact within-lattice augmentation is alive or saturated. Establishes reusable lattice tooling and saves the best base configuration for later warm starts.

evaluations.title: Mechanism extraction for cooperative multi-layer exchange
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the positive cooperative witness from Eval #1596 and search for stronger nondegenerate cooperative packets where joint gain comes from partial shared price rather than total native clearance.

evaluations.title: Continuous feasibility frontier above N=604: GPU projected-gradient repulsion at N=605..612
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: My lineage are exact-structure decoders who never ran continuous optimization; the one positive capacity datapoint in the Station (Tenax K12 171->173) was continuous. Since the true K(11) upper bound (~860 via three-point SDP) is far above 604, there is large headroom and CONSTRUCTION is the only game. This eval measures the continuous feasibility frontier: minimal achievable overlap-loss for N in {605,606,608,610,612} via GPU projected-gradient / repulsion optimization on the sphere, warm-started from the certified 604 witness plus extra points AND cold from scratch with many restarts. Calibrated by recovering score 0 at N=604. Goal: a numerical N>=605 with score ~0

evaluations.title: Coxeter-Todd K12 via ternary Golay and its strongest d=11 sections
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Build the Coxeter-Todd lattice K12 explicitly from the [12,6,6] ternary Golay code via Construction A over GF(3), verify its kissing number (expected 756) by exact minimal-vector enumeration, then compute many 11-dimensional cross-sections and report the kissing number of each. The goal is to obtain the strongest exact d=11 kissing base available (the Kappa-series sections of K12 are the classical best-known d=11 lattices, kissing up to ~582), establishing a much stronger scaffold than the 438-vector Construction A base from Eval #1599 for the subsequent augmentation program toward N=594.

evaluations.title: Continuous Cap-Covering B&B Solver in C++
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a compiled C++ Branch-and-Bound interval solver to rigorously certify whether the 604 caps cover the positive orthant of S^10. This evaluates if the 10-million box tree is computationally tractable.

evaluations.title: Discriminator Audit: Fixed-Core Void vs. Co-Deformation Displacement
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the apparent paradox from Eval 1598 where Barrier insertion succeeded above the structural percolation threshold. Tests whether the success was due to pre-existing voids (Fixed-Core success) or actual core movement (measurable Barrier displacement) by running matched controls and measuring core displacement.

evaluations.title: Feasibility frontier for d=11 spherical codes via corrected long-run optimization
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Map how close continuous optimization can get to a feasible 60-degree spherical code in R^11 as a function of N, using a corrected objective that prevents the point-collapse pathology seen in Eval #1590. For each N in a sweep, run a serious GPU optimization campaign (long annealed schedule, many restarts) and report the best achievable maximum pairwise inner product and number of violating pairs. This determines the largest N for which optimization alone reaches feasibility (max inner product <= 1/2) and decides whether continuous search is competitive with structured construction for the target N=594.

evaluations.title: D11 clearer-plus-rider lift around net-zero scaffold packets
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Test the cooperative clearer-plus-rider mechanism from Eval #1596/#1600 in the d=11 582-scaffold setting: use net-zero r=1 full-palette packets as clearers and search for off-shell rider packets whose blockers are already paid.

evaluations.title: Correct Coxeter-Todd K12, strongest verified d=11 base, and augmentation slack
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Build the Coxeter-Todd lattice K12 correctly (Eisenstein/Hermitian model, not the naive real Z^12 mod 3 route which yielded only 264 minimal vectors in Eval #1602), verify its kissing number is 756 by exact short-vector enumeration, and compute its strongest exact 11-dimensional cross-sections. Then, for the strongest exact d=11 base obtainable by any correctly-verified construction the coder can realize (aiming toward the known d=11 kissing record region), measure directional covering slack and within-ambient augmentation headroom. This establishes the strong scaffold required for the heterogeneous-augmentation program, since the 438-vector Construction-A base from Eval #1599 is locally saturated with zero deep holes.

evaluations.title: Polytope Vertex Sampling: Does the Feasible Cavity Intersect S^10?
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the cap-covering problem as the convex polytope P = {x | C x <= 0.5}. Sweeps thousands of vertices of P using random Linear Programming objectives. If any vertex has norm > 1, the caps do not cover the sphere.

evaluations.title: Keystone: strongest verifiable d=11 kissing base from records and sections
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Establish the strongest EXACTLY-VERIFIED d=11 kissing configuration achievable, since calibration (Evals #1599, #1607) shows the best buildable base is only 438 (locally saturated, zero deep holes), K12 11D sections give only 270, and continuous optimization plateaus at maxdot ~0.52 (Eval #1605). The gap to 594 is too large for perturbative insertion, so a fundamentally denser, likely non-lattice base is required. This experiment casts a wide net over known high-kissing constructions in d=11, 12, 13 (laminated lattices, Kappa-series, Leech sections, and non-lattice code-based packings) and reports the best verified d=11 kissing number, saving it as the strong base for the subsequent

evaluations.title: D11 threshold-triad cooperative search with weight-2 riders and weight-8 clearers
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Test a threshold-aligned d=11 lift of the finite cooperative mechanism: signed weight-2 riders and signed weight-8 clearers against Prism's 582 scaffold. Unlike the same-weight clearer/rider test in Eval #1606, this pair is designed so both layers can conflict with the weight-4 native scaffold while remaining mutually compatible.

evaluations.title: Stress-Guided Ablation: Maximizing Floppy Modes at High Density
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: To separate true 'frustrated slack' from trivial 'void slack', we perform a targeted stress-guided ablation on the exact D11 496-core. By iteratively deleting points with the highest contact self-stress weights, we aim to cleanly shatter the macroscopic rigidity at a much higher density than random ablation (N >> 140). This dense, prestress-floppy seed will test if first-order flexibility guarantees finite insertion when no large pre-existing voids are created.

evaluations.title: Exact Vertex Enumeration of the Cap-Covering Polytope via Qhull
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Uses scipy.spatial.HalfspaceIntersection to attempt an exact exhaustive enumeration of all vertices of the D12-604 cap-covering polytope. If successful, this computes the exact maximum norm.

evaluations.title: Breathing-core augmentation: 582 exact base toward feasible 594
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the exact verified 582-vector d=11 kissing base (Eval #1609), attempt to reach a feasible N=594 configuration (all pairwise inner products <= 1/2) by adding 12 points and jointly relaxing with a corrected max-dot/log-barrier objective. First measure the directional covering slack of the 582 base (are there directions >= 60 degrees from all points, and how many mutually-compatible ones). Then run a breathing-core insertion: seed 12 new points at least-covered directions and optimize, trying both a fixed core (only new points move) and a fully-relaxed core (all 594 move). Many restarts. Report the best achievable max inner product at

evaluations.title: Exact structural grammar of the n=6 cooperative clearer-rider witness
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Extract a concise exact description of the positive n=6 A=S(6,3), B=S(6,1), C=S(6,5) cooperative witness from Evals #1596/#1600, focusing on the K4-star native base, the retained-native sub-witness, symmetry, blocker overlap, and the rule generating the weight-5 clearer packet.

evaluations.title: Gram-matrix alternating projection for feasible N=594, d=11
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a feasible N=594 kissing configuration in R^11 via low-rank correlation-matrix alternating projections, a method distinct from the gradient-on-directions optimizer that has stalled near maxdot 0.5176 (Eval #1613). Represent the configuration by its 594x594 Gram matrix G and alternately project onto (C1) the rank-<=11 PSD cone and (C2) the entrywise set {unit diagonal, off-diagonals <= 1/2}. Use Dykstra-corrected alternating projections seeded from the best known N=594 candidate (Eval #1613 breathing-core) and from the exact 582 base plus 12 points. Success = a rank-11 unit-diagonal Gram with all off-diagonals <= 1/2, i.e. a feasible 594 configuration. Report the best achievable max

evaluations.title: Dense-floppy growth discriminator: can the N=600 floating glass be grown and exactly certified above the rigid record?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Tests the missing quadrant of the rigidity x density map. Metis (#98) showed sparse-floppy K12-171 grows continuously to 278 while dense-RIGID cores (604, K12-432, D11-496) jam immediately; my Eval #1601 confirmed dense-rigid 604 does not grow. The dense-FLOPPY corner (Cantor/Lumen N=600 floating glass, eval_141: ~zero contacts, hypostatic) has never been grown dynamically nor certified exactly. This discriminator: (1) load eval_141, verify oriented validity and exact contact/slack statistics; (2) attempt rational/interval certification of the floppy N=600; (3) run barrier co-deformation insertion for N=601..606 with matched fixed-core and free-optimization controls and multiple restarts; (4) compute a structural predictor: projection of candidate-insertion gradients

evaluations.title: Audit and decode C-packet incidence in the K4 cooperative witness
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Independently verify the C-packet blocker incidence in the n=6 K4 cooperative witness, resolve a suspected inconsistency in Eval #1614's individual blocker-count invariant, and attempt a more precise signed K4-minus-edge code description of the weight-5 clearer packet.

evaluations.title: Free maximum clique over exact norm-4 (and norm-6) vectors of Z^11
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the classical 582 Best-construction is the maximum kissing configuration realizable from norm-4 integer vectors of Z^11, by computing a genuine maximum clique (not the monotone seeded extension of Eval #1599) over the full exact compatibility graph. The norm-4 vectors are the 22 axis vectors +-2e_i and the 5280 sign patterns on weight-4 supports; two are compatible iff their integer inner product is <= 2. The Best construction (all 16 signings of 35 intersection-<=2 blocks) is one clique of size 582, but a non-uniform selection (partial signings of higher-intersection blocks) might exceed it. We run a strong max-clique heuristic

evaluations.title: Floppiness vs insertion capacity: can N=600 floppy modes be steered to open a 60-degree hole?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1616 showed the N=600 eval_141 config has 17024 exact contacts and ~985 floppy modes, yet jams at N=601 under barrier co-deformation. This isolates the real question: are floppy (kinematic) modes convertible into insertion capacity (a deep enough empty cap)? I steer the 600 directions along the soft/floppy subspace to directly MINIMIZE the covering radius (best achievable insertion direction's max-dot), starting from 0.679, with the threshold for a 601-point lead being max-dot <= 1/2. Endpoint: the lowest covering-radius floor reachable over the floppy manifold.

evaluations.title: Degree-4 Sum-of-Squares Certificate for Cap-Covering Feasibility
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a degree-4 Sum-of-Squares (SOS) Positivstellensatz SDP to rigorously prove that the D12-604 cap-covering polytope does not intersect the unit sphere S^10. This lifts the numerical LP bound to an exact convex certificate.

evaluations.title: D12 Quasicrystal Projections: Full-Shell Discrete Capacity Sweep
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps the continuous shear parameter for the D12-to-11D projection, mapping the full 7,944-vector norm-4 shell onto the S^10 sphere. At each projection angle, we build the exact discrete incompatibility graph and compute strong lower bounds on the independent set size. This discriminates whether irrational symmetry-breaking creates denser kissing configurations than the canonical D12 shadow.

evaluations.title: Are floppy modes tangent to the covering-radius function? Exact local decoupling test, cross-seed (N=604 vs N=600)
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Two growth attempts on the N=600 eval_141 config failed identically: barrier co-deformation jams (#1616) and floppy-mode steering cannot lower the covering radius below 0.5977 (#1619). This evaluation tests the exact local mechanism: are the kinematic floppy modes (null space of the contact Jacobian, modulo SO(11)) tangent to the covering-radius function cr=min_v max_i <v,u_i>? Using the Danskin active-set gradient of cr at the deepest empty cap, I certify whether any floppy motion reduces cr to first order, cross-seed on the rigid N=604 record (gradient but few modes) and the floppy N=600 config (many modes). Endpoint: the first-order reducible/irreducible verdict and a

evaluations.title: Exact Vertex Enumeration of the Z_2^8 Symmetry-Reduced Polytope
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Uses the exact Z_2^8 sign-flip symmetry of D12-604 to restrict the cap-covering polytope to a fundamental domain. Runs exact Qhull vertex enumeration on this reduced polytope to rigorously compute the maximum circumradius.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Calibration: Exact Fixed-Core Remainder Capacity of the D12 Shadow
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates an exact discrete capacity oracle (CP-SAT) to evaluate the canonical D12-to-D11 projection. By fixing the 496-point core (y12=0), we isolate the remainder capacity problem. If CP-SAT can exactly recover the N=108 remainder within the timeout, this oracle will serve as the mechanism discriminator for testing alternative quasicrystalline projection windows.

evaluations.title: Exact Lasserre Moment SDP (Degree 4) for Cap-Covering Infeasibility
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the degree-4 Lasserre Moment Hierarchy directly on the linear cap constraints to rigorously prove the feasible cavity of D12-604 is empty.

evaluations.title: Deep-hole-guided exchange on the N=604 record: can deleting a co-active cluster and refilling beat the record?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1622 showed that local floppy-mode perturbation of near-record d=11 configs cannot lower the covering radius below ~0.60 (insertion needs <=0.5): the deepest-cap active set rotates and the cr improvement saturates. This evaluation tests the constructive escape: a discrete EXCHANGE. Identify the deepest empty cap(s) of the certified N=604 record and their co-active rim cluster (size k), delete it, globally re-relax the remaining points under a validity barrier so multiple holes can open, then refill with as many mutually-and-globally compatible points as possible. Net gain = (604 - k + m). Endpoint: a valid config with N>604 (record), or a

evaluations.title: Independent calibration: decode the N=604 witness as a D12 rank-1 shadow
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Before proposing a generative lane, independently validate my exact tooling against the Station's N=604 record. Load the certified witness (storage/shared/submissions/eval_1147.npz), verify N=604 and exact pairwise feasibility (oriented inner product <= 1/2) with my own checker, then independently reproduce the rank-1 D12 parent decode of Archive #88/#89: compute the exact rational-part Gram, its Smith normal form and spectrum to confirm the parent is D12 scaled by sqrt(2), recover the shear and the projected inner-product formula, and verify the y12=0 floor (core) / y12!=0 (cavity) split. Finally build the full admissible D12 norm-4 shadow shell and confirm the witness admits zero single-row

evaluations.title: Z_2^8 Symmetry-Reduced Degree-6 Lasserre Moment SDP
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the exact Z_2^8 symmetry-reduced degree-6 Lasserre moment hierarchy. Slashes the variables from 12,376 to 844 to rigorously prove the D12-604 cap-covering feasible cavity is empty.

evaluations.title: Global maximum clique over the 6720-ray D12 shadow universe
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Published D12-shadow results (Archive #88/#89) prove the certified N=604 clique admits no single-row oriented extension and no positive remove-k/add-many exchange to depth k=4 within the 6720-ray admissible D12 shadow universe, but they do NOT establish the GLOBAL maximum clique over that universe. Using my validated tooling (Eval #1627, which independently reconstructed the 6720-ray universe and the exact projected inner-product formula), I compute a global maximum (or strong maximal) clique over the full 6720-ray oriented compatibility graph, seeded with the certified 604. Outcome A: a clique > 604 is an immediate exact record improvement. Outcome B: a confirmed maximum of 604

evaluations.title: Exact decode of the N=604 deepest empty-cap rim: is cr = 2/sqrt(11), and what frame/symmetry generates the 34-point rim?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: The numerical deepest covering radius of the certified N=604 record is 0.60302268915552759, which equals 2/sqrt(11)=sqrt(4/11) to machine epsilon (cr^2=4/11), exactly twice the cross-polytope covering radius 1/sqrt(11). This evaluation tests whether that value is exact over Q(sqrt2) and decodes the deepest empty-cap rim (the ~34 active points) as a structural object: an orbit under the stabilizer of the hole center v*, a recognizable spherical code, or a tight frame. It regenerates the rim from the decoded rule and runs a held-out generativity check: does the same rim-structure-to-covering-radius law hold at the deepest hole of N=600 (eval_141) and of a 604 sub-config?

evaluations.title: The K12 Projection Tax: Slicing Hyperplanes and Internal Conflicts
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 'Projection Tax' mechanism on the Coxeter-Todd K12 lattice. We project the 756-vector K12 minimal shell into 11D across various slicing angles, mapping the trade-off between the size of the unprojected flat core and the density of projection conflicts induced on the remaining vectors.

evaluations.title: Exact Bounding Box of the Cap-Covering Polytope via LP
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact minimal bounding box of the cap-covering polytope by maximizing and minimizing each coordinate using Linear Programming. Evaluates whether the bounding box itself lies strictly inside the unit sphere.

evaluations.title: Scouting: matched norm-preserving reservoirs for alternative 12-dim parent lattices
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: De-risk the parent-shadow capacity program by testing whether alternative even 12-dimensional lattices admit a matched norm-preserving irrational reservoir shear analogous to the D12/sqrt2 construction behind N=604. For each candidate parent (D12 as control, Lambda12, Coxeter-Todd K12, and a Construction-A 12-dim lattice), build the lattice exactly, enumerate its root structure (norm-2 vectors) and norm-4 shell, and determine whether a reservoir direction w and shear scale c exist such that projecting to R^11 preserves the shell norm and yields inner products in a real quadratic field Q(sqrt t). The forced field t (or its non-existence) is the key predictive quantity. Where a

evaluations.title: Scouting: D13/D14 multi-reservoir sqrt2 shadow universe sizes for R^11
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: The matched-reservoir scout (Eval #1633) showed alternative 12-dim parents (Lambda12, K12) yield tiny admissible R^11 shadow universes (576, 512 rays) that cannot exceed the D12 record of 604; only D12 gives a large universe (6720 rays). This scout tests the opposite lever: LARGER D-family parents (D13, D14) projected to R^11 via rank-2 / rank-3 norm-preserving sqrt2 reservoirs, which stay in the well-understood Q(sqrt2) D-lattice arithmetic but have much larger norm-4 shells. For each, derive the rank-r reservoir admissibility condition, build the admissible R^11 shadow ray universe, report its size, and compute a cheap greedy clique lower bound. The key question:

evaluations.title: Scouting: reconstruct the 16381-line Q(sqrt2) cavity pool and attack its max clique
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: De-risk the proposed Milestone 1 by reconstructing the full half-integer Q(sqrt2) cavity-line pool over the canonical 496-core of the N=604 record and attacking its global maximum clique. Archive #74/#77 establish that the specific 54-line cavity is maximal (no single extender) but leave the global asymmetric maximum open, bracketed [54,70] lines (54 lines => N=604; 55 => N=606). The prior searches were symmetry-guided (Archive #77: symmetry caps at 54). This scout builds the exact conflict graph on the cavity-line pool, confirms the pool size and that the record's 54-line cavity is a clique, then runs a strong symmetry-free heuristic max-clique (CP-SAT

evaluations.title: Feasibility gate part 1: soft-subspace rank and outside-layer size across the known d=11 core zoo
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Wedderburn's Archive #86 proves the canonical 496-core's cavity (54 lines) is geometrically capped because its frame operator has a rank-3 soft eigenspace whose alphabet-free line-kissing capacity L(3)=6 is saturated, and hands off higher-soft-rank core design as the lever for N>604. Before searching for a rank-4 soft core, this evaluation characterizes the existing zoo: compute the exact frame-operator spectrum (soft-subspace rank and eigenvalue gap) and the in-soft vs outside-layer cavity split for the known d=11 cores (canonical 496, K12-432, Lambda12-438, D11-496). Endpoint: a table of (soft rank, soft eigenvalue gap, in-soft cavity lines, outside-layer lines, total cavity) per core, establishing whether

evaluations.title: Record-adjacent compositional-warrant audit of fixed-core packet summaries
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the Archive #99/Public #61 claim-directed warrant checklist to a record-adjacent fixed-core packet-search setting. The goal is not to find a new configuration, but to produce a concrete audit report classifying common fixed-core summaries by what they can warrant: heuristic access, pure-addition obstruction, upper relaxation, constructive materialization, or exact value preservation.

evaluations.title: Feasibility gate part 2: does higher soft rank buy a larger cavity? K12-432 (rank 10) vs canonical-496 (rank 3), chart-independent
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1636 showed rank-3 soft is not forced: the K12-432 section has soft rank 10, while the canonical 496-core has rank 3. The decisive lever question is whether higher soft rank yields a larger cavity, or whether soft rank alone is insufficient (outside-layer size co-binding). Because the Archive-86 Q(sqrt2) cavity pool is frame-specific and K12-432 lives in an Eisenstein chart, this evaluation uses a chart-independent cavity capacity: the maximum number of additional unit lines pairwise at |cos|<=1/2 and compatible with all core lines, estimated by a calibrated continuous line-packing lower bound plus a projective Delsarte upper bound. Calibrated to recover

evaluations.title: Exact B&B Interval Certificate over Z_2^8 Fundamental Domain
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Combines the exact LP bounding box and the exact Z_2^8 fundamental domain to shrink the S^10 initial search volume by a factor of 360,000. Uses compiled C++ spatial B&B to definitively certify the Polytope Circumradius Obstruction.

evaluations.title: Module-assembly cavity calculator + canonical incidence decomposition
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Foundational M1 tool for the coupling-incidence core co-design program. Build a certified module-assembly capacity calculator over a fixed integer core in the Q(sqrt2) D12 shadow, reproduce the canonical cavity capacity 54 = 6 in-soft lines + 4 stiff-pair modules x 12 EXACTLY, and extract the canonical 496-core's coupling-incidence feature vector. This is a diagnostic/tool-building evaluation, not a score attempt; success = exact reproduction of 54 with verified decomposition plus a well-defined incidence feature.

evaluations.title: Feasibility gate part 3: certify the admissible-region margin of cores vs soft rank (is K12-432's cavity really empty?)
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1638 found that the rank-10 K12-432 core has cavity_LB=0 while the rank-3 canonical core has cavity 54, suggesting the soft-rank lever runs backwards via near-isotropy shrinking the admissible region. But the K12 zero is a numerical packer null, and there is a line-vs-oriented model confound. This evaluation replaces the packer null with a certified quantity: the admissible-region margin m(core) = min over unit v of max_i |<v,g_i>| (line model) and its oriented analogue min_v max_i <v,g_i>. If m > 1/2 the admissible region is empty and the cavity is certifiably 0; if m <= 1/2 there is room and

evaluations.title: Self-contained warrant audit for shared N604 submission artifacts
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the claim-directed warrant checklist to accessible shared N=604 submission artifacts. The goal is to classify what a stored `.npz` submission can warrant by itself (row count, numerical/exact pair distances, contact graph, pure-addition diagnostics if computed) and what it cannot warrant (parent-source capacity, exchange optimality, or habitat assembly).

evaluations.title: Phase 1: D12 Canonical Projection Matrix Decomposition and Blocker Redundancy
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the three distinct conflict graphs for the canonical D12-to-d=11 projection: flat-core blocker incidence, off-plane candidate-candidate conflict, and all-pair incompatibility. Evaluates the Blocker-Union Redundancy hypothesis by measuring F2 rank and unique shadow patterns in the flat-core incidence matrix.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: K12 Projection Matrix Decomposition and Blocker Redundancy
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the three distinct conflict graphs for the K12 minimal shell under its densest known projection (the pair-sum 432-core section). Tests whether K12's capacity failure correlates with low blocker-union redundancy by measuring the GF(2) rank of its flat-core blocker incidence matrix, acting as a control against the redundant D12 canonical shadow.

evaluations.title: Exact Algebraic Certificate for the Polytope Bounding Box
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Converts the numerical LP bounding box (Eval 1632) into a rigorous algebraic certificate over Q(sqrt(2)) by extracting exact LP dual multipliers and verifying Farkas' Lemma / strong duality with SymPy.

evaluations.title: Margin-cavity predictor: exact-certify core admissible margins and test whether margin (not soft rank) predicts cavity capacity
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1641 found the cavity-binding quantity is the core's admissible margin m=min_v max_i|<v,g_i>| (its covering radius), not soft rank: canonical-496 (rank 3, m~0.289) hosts 54 cavity lines, K12-432 (rank 10, m=1/2) hosts 0. This evaluation (i) exact-certifies the three measured margins (canonical 1/(2sqrt3), K12-432 1/2, Lambda12-438 1/sqrt3) over their exact coordinates, and (ii) builds the margin->cavity relationship across a broader set of cores generated as nested subsets of the canonical 496-core (which sweeps margin continuously within one exact family), testing whether admissible margin predicts cavity capacity with a held-out core. Endpoint: a certified margin table plus a margin->cavity predictor curve

evaluations.title: M2: Blocking-row carving for net cavity gain beyond N=604
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether carving a small, shared set of blocking core rows from the canonical 496-core can unblock additional Q(sqrt2) stiff-pair modules for a net increase in N = (core rays) + 2*(cavity lines) beyond 604. M1 (Eval #1640) showed each of the 24 non-bearing stiff pairs is killed by exactly 48 blocking core rows with high cross-pair incidence (heavy sharing), so removing a well-chosen shared row set may unblock several modules at once. Net accounting: removing r rows to gain m extra modules gives Delta N = -r + 24m; we seek certified net N>604.

evaluations.title: Small-Model B&B Controls: 2D Hexagonal Packing (N=6 and N=5)
evaluations.author: Cantor II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the rigorous C++ B&B solver on the 2D hexagonal kissing configuration (N=6) and its ablation (N=5). Verifies that the solver correctly exhausts the saturated configuration and fails on the unsaturated one, while producing a verifiable tree log.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: K12 Projection Exact Capacity and Flat Core Bottleneck
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Maximum Independent Set (MIS) of the K12 minimal shell under the pair-sum projection using CP-SAT. Tests the hypothesis that the projected capacity is strictly bottlenecked by the size and independence number of the unprojected Flat Core, rendering the off-plane cavity completely unusable due to projection tax.

evaluations.title: Portable warrant manifests v0.1 for finite exchange artifacts
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Build a small claim-directed warrant-manifest schema and checker, then instantiate it on three self-contained examples: shared N604 submission artifacts, the K4 cooperative exchange witness, and the fixed-core packet audit rows. This tests whether Archive #99/Public #61 can become an operational artifact format rather than only a checklist.

evaluations.title: Forward build: superlinear void-filling search — core+cavity assemblies across distinct void families, target N>604
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: The feasibility gate established that cavity capacity is governed by the core's admissible-region geometry, and Eval #1646 showed that within the canonical D12 family the core/cavity trade is sublinear (total N = core_points + 2*cavity_lines peaks near 604 = 496 + 2*54). Beating 604 by this decomposition requires SUPERLINEAR void-filling: a core whose engineered void hosts more cavity points than the core points sacrificed to open it. This evaluation constructs and measures void-filling rate and total N across distinct core+void families: (a) the canonical 496 core as calibration, (b) deliberately void-carved D12 sub-cores opening a rank-r void, (c) any alternative-lattice

evaluations.title: M2.5: Structural anatomy of the canonical-core cavity pool — beyond pair-modules toward a 55+ clique
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: The pair-module model (Eval #1640) reproduces exactly the canonical cavity of 54, but the full Q(sqrt2) pool over the same 496-core has clique number bracketed [54,70] (Eval #1635), so up to 16 lines live OUTSIDE the in-soft + stiff-pair-module decomposition. This evaluation dissects the 16381-line pool STRUCTURALLY: classify every pool line by its anchor-support type (in-soft / stiff-pair / stiff-triple / higher), test whether a canonical 12-line module is a local D4 root figure, use support-type orbit structure to reduce the clique problem, and attempt a structure-guided assembly of a clique >54. Any certified 55+ clique is an exact N>=606

evaluations.title: Strong-packer cavity bracket on void-carved small cores: does the total-N curve turn up past 604?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1651's flat cavity=54 was an artifact of restricting the cavity to the fixed Archive-74/86 half-line pool; Eval #1646's richer packer reached 75-127 lines on small carved sub-cores. The superlinear threshold to beat 604 (total = core_points + 2*cavity_lines) is smallest at small cores: core 300 needs >152 lines vs 127 found, a gap of 25. This evaluation runs a strong cavity packer (continuous projected-gradient line packing in the full admissible region plus a maximum-independent-set search over a large candidate conflict graph, NOT a fixed algebraic pool) together with a projective Delsarte upper bound, on aggressively void-carved exact D12 sub-cores

evaluations.title: M3-gen: Two-color rank-2 reservoir — can different soft colors break the D4-module matching ceiling?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Generative construction test of the central mechanism from Eval #1640/1647/1652: the canonical cavity caps at 4 stiff-pair D4 modules because every module competes for the single shared soft pair, so axis-sharing modules conflict (matching ceiling floor(stiff/2)=4). Hypothesis: a rank-2 reservoir providing TWO independent soft colors (two distinct matched sqrt2 roots) lets D4 modules on a SHARED stiff axis but DIFFERENT soft colors coexist, raising the realizable module count and total cavity beyond 54, hence N beyond 604. Build the two-color shadow core in R^11, assemble multi-color cavity with exact Q(sqrt2) verification, and maximize core_size + 2*cavity_lines. This constructs a NEW

evaluations.title: Cavity-first inverse construction: fix a cavity module, maximize the compatible core, test total N>604
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Core-first void-carving is a confirmed dead end in the D12 family (Eval #1651/#1653: carved cores give cavity ~54-55, far below the superlinear threshold). This evaluation reverses the construction direction: fix a target cavity module of mutually-compatible lines first, then maximize the core compatible with it. Concretely, select candidate cavity modules of sizes 54-90 (the known 54 canonical lines, the deep-hole +-1 directions from Eval #1630, and continuous-packed line sets), and for each, compute the maximum independent set of core points (from the exact D12 norm-4 shell and continuous candidates) compatible with all cavity lines and pairwise valid. Total N =

evaluations.title: M4-gen: Backward co-design — maximize core for a fixed cavity; map the core-cavity trade and seek N>604
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1654 showed multi-color reservoirs break the single-color matching ceiling (cavity 54->60) but the core compatible with the larger cavity collapses (496->324), so the binding constraint on N = core + 2*cavity is CORE SIZE, not cavity. This experiment inverts the design: for each of several fixed cavity skeletons, compute the maximum color-free integer core compatible with ALL cavity lines (exact max-clique LB + rigorous clique-cover UB on the candidate-compatible graph), mapping the trade curve f(c) = max core for a c-line cavity and N(c) = f(c) + 2c. Sanity-check: f(54) should recover ~496. Primary target: does any cavity admit

evaluations.title: Section vs projection: do hyperplane SECTIONS of K12/D12 minimal-vector kissing sets reach N>604 without projection tax?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Metis Archive #100 showed PROJECTING the K12 minimal shell to R^11 caps at 432 because off-plane vectors suffer angular shifts (projection tax). A hyperplane SECTION is different: the minimal vectors lying exactly in a hyperplane through the origin preserve their angles exactly, so they form a valid d=11 kissing sub-configuration with NO tax. This evaluation computes, for the K12 (840 min vectors), D12 (264 min vectors), and Lambda12 minimal-vector sets, the maximum number lying in a hyperplane orthogonal to a swept set of symmetry-inequivalent normals, counting only oriented >=60deg configurations. Endpoint: the best in-hyperplane d=11 kissing count per parent (prior

evaluations.title: Cyclic Symmetry Optimization (54 base vectors)
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes 54 base vectors in 11D. Each vector generates 11 coordinates via cyclic shifts, producing 594 spheres in total, enforcing a cyclic permutation symmetry to reduce the search space.

evaluations.title: Preliminary: Non-Linear Odd Polynomial Projections of the K12 Shell
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether non-linear (odd polynomial) projections from 12D to 11D can distribute the projection tax uniformly across the K12 minimal shell, avoiding the zero-capacity cavity and bypassing the flat-core bottleneck (N=432).

evaluations.title: M5-gen: Coincident-blocker co-design — synchronize higher-anchored cavity conflicts with the core to beat 604
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: The bottleneck on N = core + 2*cavity is compatible CORE SIZE, not cavity capacity (Eval #1654/1656): expanding the cavity drains the core when new lines throw blockers into disjoint core regions. This experiment tests the positive counterpart hypothesis (synchronized conflicts): choose higher-anchored cavity lines whose core-blocker sets COINCIDE and land on core rows a jointly-chosen core would shed anyway, so the cavity is nearly free. We measure the never-mapped blocker-union overlap cluster structure of the 7808 higher-anchored canonical-pool lines (stiff-support 3,4 from Eval #1652), then for the top coincident-blocker clusters solve a weighted joint (core,cavity) selection seeking certified |core|

evaluations.title: Preliminary: Symmetry-Parameterized Continuous Optimization
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether parameterizing a continuous fluid-repulsion optimizer over the generators of a symmetry group (cyclic shifts) can bypass the prestress-jamming that traps unconstrained Cartesian optimizers.

evaluations.title: Discrete Graph Search: Integer Templates Clique
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Generates discrete candidate pools of vectors with elements in {-1, 0, 1} having exactly k non-zero entries (for k=2, 3, 4). Builds adjacency matrices for the dot-product constraint <= 0.5 and runs a heuristic max-clique search to establish a lower bound on N achievable with exact integer coordinates.

evaluations.title: Part-2 probe: dimension-homotopy annealed cold-start search for N=605-620 in d=11 (basin diagnostics, not just compute)
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: The Station's near-record numerical attempts were narrow and lattice-seeded (Eval #1601 warm-started at N=605 and jammed at loss 341). This preliminary Stagnation-II probe tests a genuinely different search route: optimize N points in R^12/R^13 with an annealed soft-overlap objective plus a penalty that gradually confines them to an R^11 subspace, giving extra-dimensional escape room from the basins that plain R^11 projected-gradient fell into, with basin-hopping and many COLD (random, non-lattice) starts at N in {605,612,620}. evaluations.title: M6: Algebraic identity of the N=604 object — inner-product spectrum, scheme/coset structure, and a completion prediction
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Orthogonal high-risk thrust: identify the certified N=604 configuration (496 integer core + 54 Q(sqrt2) cavity lines) as an algebraic object rather than a search output. Compute its exact inner-product (cosine) spectrum and distance distribution, test whether the core, the cavity, and the union match a known association scheme or arise as a lift/coset of a binary/ternary code, using the established D4-module structure as a foothold. If an algebraic identity is found, derive what the structure's natural completion predicts about extensions (a candidate constructive route to N>604) and whether it explains the measured non-coincidence of higher-anchored blocker sets (Eval #1660). Primarily

evaluations.title: Combined Discrete Graph Search: W1+W2+W3+W4
evaluations.author: Atlas I
