evaluations.abstract: Generates discrete candidate pools W1, W2, W3, and W4 (vectors with elements in {-1, 0, 1} and exactly 1, 2, 3, or 4 non-zero entries). Combines them into a single unified graph of size 6842 to find the maximum possible exact integer-coordinate clique.

evaluations.title: M7-gen: Minimal soft-subspace (s=2) single-root shadow — close the module-count lever and diagnose the third soft axis
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: The central structural law emerging from M1-M6: within single-root sqrt2 D12-shadows, the number of D4-modules is at most the matching number of the stiff axes = floor((11-s)/2), where s = dim of the soft subspace. The canonical shadow has s=3 (soft triple {2,7,9}) despite a single shear root spanning only 2 axes {7,9} — the third soft axis is unexplained. I tested LARGER soft (two-color, Eval #1654, lost core); this experiment tests MINIMAL soft: construct an s=2 single-root shadow (soft = exactly the two shear axes, third soft axis avoided if possible), diagnose whether the third soft axis is forced

evaluations.title: Preliminary: Quadratic Fibrations of the D12 Shell and Spectrum Sharpness
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether mapping 1D antipodal fibers of the D12 norm-4 shell to single points in S^10 via structured quadratic fibrations can preserve a sharp, discrete algebraic spectrum (a 'comb'), avoiding the continuous smear of naive distortions.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Seed Epitaxy: Growing the 530-Vector Crystal
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the 530-vector exact integer clique (W1+W4) discovered in Eval 1665 as a rigid, frozen seed. Initializes 64 free vectors and runs continuous optimization with repulsion loss to extend the configuration to the target N=594.

evaluations.title: Manifested cooperation readiness audit for existing finite layers
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the v0.1 warrant-manifest checker with a composition-readiness test. Apply it to existing examples: the exact K4 cooperative witness as a positive control, shared N604 artifacts as a negative source-layer control, fixed-core shadow3 A/B rows as a historical record-adjacent control, and K12 flat/off-plane data if accessible. The goal is to see whether manifests can reveal actionable untested layer compositions or missing fields, not to search for new candidates.

evaluations.title: Quadratic Fibrations of the K12 Shell: Testing Spectrum Sharpness
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Applying structured quadratic fibrations to the K12 minimal shell to determine if non-linear fiber maps can preserve a discrete algebraic spectrum (a 'comb') on lattices that otherwise fail due to linear flat-core bottlenecks.

evaluations.title: Symmetrized Channeling Fibrations: Recovering Antipodal Capacity on D12, K12, Lambda12
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Quadratic fibrations (even maps) quotient the parent shell by the antipodal map, halving the apparent capacity. We test whether explicitly symmetrizing the mapped image (Y U -Y) recovers kissing capacity while preserving the sharp discrete algebraic spectrum (the 'comb'). We apply Map A to D12, K12, and Lambda12 to benchmark spectrum preservation and exact MIS.

evaluations.title: Alphabet Discovery: Clustering Continuous Coordinates
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the float64 vectors from the cyclic symmetry continuous optimization (Eval 1658) to identify the empirical distribution of coordinate values. The goal is to discover the underlying discrete alphabet (e.g., fractions or algebraic numbers) required for N=594.

evaluations.title: Channeling Fibrations on Lambda12: Maximizing Capacity under Spectrum Preservation
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that integer-coordinate parent lattices (Lambda12) naturally preserve sharp algebraic spectra under quadratic cross-term fibrations, we test a battery of mapping topologies on Lambda12 to find a fibration that maximizes MIS capacity while maintaining a strict discrete comb (< 20 unique values).

evaluations.title: Permutohedron group-orbit codes for d=11: exact oriented capacity of S_12 shells vs Steiner/M_12 sub-orbits
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary exploration (Stagnation II, approved by supervisor) of a non-lattice construction primitive for the d=11 kissing problem: group-orbit codes built from the deleted permutation representation on 12 points (the 11-dim irrep shared by S_12, M_12, PSL(2,11)). Indicator vectors of k-subsets, projected to the sum-zero hyperplane (exactly R^11), have rational Gram matrices governed entirely by set-intersection numbers. We compute, in exact arithmetic, the oriented kissing capacity (largest pairwise cos<=1/2 subset) of single full S_12 shells (lattice A_11 shells, as calibration) and of sporadic Steiner/M_12 sub-orbits, and test whether Golay/Steiner coherence lets multiple shells STACK into one simultaneously compatible code where generic

evaluations.title: M8: Close f(54) — exact maximum core compatible with the canonical 54-line cavity (record if >496)
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: My Archive #102 leaves open the maximum integer core compatible with the canonical 54-line Q(sqrt2) cavity: bracketed f(54) in [496,528] (Eval #1656). A core of size >=497 compatible with all 54 canonical cavity lines is an immediate certified N>604 (e.g. 500 core + 54 cavity = 608); closing it at 496 resolves one of the paper's two open brackets. This is a single targeted exact maximum-independent-set computation on the candidate set of norm-4 integer rays compatible with all 54 cavity lines, accelerated by the configuration's exact symmetry (coordinate-permutation/sign group), seeking either a certified record core or a closed exact bound.

evaluations.title: Expanded Discrete Graph Search: W5 and W6 Ternary Vectors
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the discrete kissing number configuration capacity of high-weight ternary vectors. Generates Pool W5 (exactly 5 non-zero elements in {-1, 1}) and Pool W6 (exactly 6 non-zero elements). Constructs conflict graphs based on dot product > 0.5 constraint, and uses a heuristic maximal clique solver to find the largest exact subsets.

evaluations.title: Exact Classification of K12 Map C: Algebraic Spectrum and Code Structure
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Consolidation phase: We exactify and mathematically classify the pristine, 162-vector, conflict-free object generated by Map C (pole-anchored cross-terms) on the K12 minimal shell (Eval 1670). We compute its exact algebraic Gram spectrum, support structure, and possible equivalence to known spherical codes.

evaluations.title: Native-R^11 Burer-Monteiro feasibility solver: calibration gate — can it recover a zero-loss N=604 from scratch?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Calibration gate for a new construction object: native-R^11 low-rank Gram feasibility via Burer-Monteiro. We optimize U in R^{N x 11} with unit-norm rows to satisfy pairwise oriented compatibility <u_i,u_j> <= 1/2, minimizing a hinge-squared violation loss directly in 11 dimensions (no extra-dimensional confinement, which failed in Eval #1663). Before any N>604 attempt, we must verify the solver can recover a FEASIBLE (zero-loss) N=604 configuration FROM SCRATCH (random init, no lattice seed). This single gating evaluation answers exactly that. Success = reaching machine-zero violation at N=604 from random starts; failure = a method too weak to trust, which would stop the

evaluations.title: Portable D4-module matching warrant manifest for the N604 cavity count
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Build and test a portable warrant manifest for the D4-module matching mechanism reported in Archive #102. This is a non-score tooling/verification evaluation: the goal is not to find a new kissing configuration, but to determine whether the cavity-count mechanism can be represented as a reusable, claim-directed manifest with exact verifier hooks and explicit missing-field/non-claim boundaries.

evaluations.title: Cross-Compatibility Audit: Non-Linear K12 Quotients vs Linear Cores
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the exact cross-compatibility between the 162-vector K12 Map C non-linear quotient spherical code and two standard linear cores (the 432 K12 flat core and the 496 D11 canonical integer core). This tests whether quotient-derived codes can act as stable cavities to extend known rigid scaffolds.

evaluations.title: M9-gen: Root-system motif taxonomy of the cavity pool — do non-D4 motifs pack beyond the matching ceiling?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #102 established that the canonical cavity is built from stiff-pair sqrt2-scaled D4 root-system modules, matching-capped at 4. The generative question for N>604 is what motif could REPLACE the D4 module. This experiment classifies the higher-anchored cavity-pool lines (stiff-support 3,4) into motif types by their exact root-system Gram signature, and for each non-D4 type measures (i) the packing number of mutually compatible copies versus the D4 matching ceiling of 4, and (ii) a positive core-synchronization criterion: whether the type's blocker fibers concentrate on a small shared core region (so a jointly-chosen core could shed exactly those rows). Any motif type

evaluations.title: Orbit Graph Search: Broad Alphabet Cyclic Orbits
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for a 54-clique in an 'Orbit Graph'. Nodes represent base vectors whose 11 cyclic shifts are mutually non-overlapping. Edges connect two base vectors if their full cyclic orbits are mutually non-overlapping. Explores a broader alphabet {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} to bypass the ternary alphabet saturation.

evaluations.title: Quotient Scaffold Interstitial Packing: Continuous Optimization around the K12 Map C Core
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Having established the K12 Map C quotient object as a sparse, conflict-free 162-vector scaffold (max inner product 5/13), we test its task relevance by using it as a fixed core for continuous interstitial packing. We aim to determine if the large void slack below the 1/2 threshold allows a continuous fluid optimizer to pack enough interstitial vectors to exceed N=604.

evaluations.title: Exact Classification of Lambda12 Map D: Algebraic Spectrum and Code Structure
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Consolidation phase: We exactify and mathematically classify the 98-vector, explicitly symmetrized quotient code generated by Map D (Skip-1 Cross-Terms) on the Lambda12 minimal shell (Eval 1673). We compute its exact algebraic Gram spectrum, support structure, and automorphism group.

evaluations.title: M10-gen: Native sqrt3 grammar probe — is the matching cap a property of (sqrt2,D4) or portable?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #102 established a matching ceiling floor(stiff/2)=4 on the sqrt2-scaled D4 cavity modules of the N=604 record. This single focused probe asks whether that matching LAW is a property of the (sqrt2, D4) pairing or a portable phenomenon, by constructing a NATIVE sqrt3 grammar end-to-end: a 12-dim parent whose norm form natively matches a sqrt3 (Eisenstein/hexagonal) reservoir, its OWN matched integer core, and its NATIVE cavity motif, with the motif's root-system type and packing rule measured on its own core (NOT grafted onto the sqrt2 core - correcting the scope error of Eval #1633/1634). Primary scientific output: does a native

evaluations.title: Cross-dimensional source-grammar census of kissing optima: is generative sufficiency (contact-graph determinacy) the invariant that separates algebraically-forced optima from floppy ones?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: A cross-dimensional exact-arithmetic census of known kissing optima (d=2..8 root-system minimal vectors, d=3 icosahedron over Q(sqrt5), and the d=11 N=604 record) measuring a uniform panel of exact invariants: kissing number N, pair inner-product palette (s-distance number and values), Gram number-field degree, contact-graph edge count, and — the central novel invariant — GENERATIVE SUFFICIENCY: the rigidity-matrix rank of the contact (60-degree) graph and the resulting realization-space dimension, i.e. whether the configuration is determined up to O(d) by its contact graph (rigid/forced) or admits a positive-dimensional family (floppy). The hypothesis under test, motivated by Archive #93 (604 is rigid) and the d=3

evaluations.title: Exploration-stage nonlinear quotient growth pilot around the K12 quadratic code
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded object-generating pilot for the Q42 nonlinear-fibration lane. The evaluation should materialize or reconstruct Metis's 162-vector K12 quadratic quotient code, attach an exploration-stage passport with explicit creative debt, and test whether a finite interstitial candidate universe can grow the code when the old linear cores are abandoned. This is not a broad optimizer and not a claimed d=11 solution.

evaluations.title: Accessibility control: does from-scratch continuous search recover floppy kissing configs but fail on rigid ones, controlling for (d,N)?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Calibrated control testing the central mechanism from the source-grammar census (Eval #1686): that generic from-scratch continuous search can recover FLOPPY kissing configurations (positive-dimensional realization manifold, large descent basin) but fails on RIGID ones (isolated combinatorial solution pinned by an exact contact graph), and that this rigidity status predicts search accessibility better than dimension or count alone. We run many random-start descents on a panel of targets with KNOWN exact rigidity status from the census (floppy: d=3 N=12 icosahedral target and deliberately sub-maximal counts with slack; rigid: d=4 N=24, d=5 N=40, and larger) and measure the fraction of starts reaching a

evaluations.title: Quotient Scaffold Interstitial Packing: Exact Algebraic Candidates from K12 Higher Shells
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Having proven that continuous fluid optimizers jam when packing the exact 162-vector K12 Map C quotient scaffold (Eval 1683), we test a discrete algebraic interstitial pool. We apply Map C to the higher shells of K12 (norm-6 and norm-8) to generate an algebraically commensurate candidate alphabet (the denominator-13 field). We test the exact bipartite compatibility of these higher-shell candidates against the fixed 162-vector core.

evaluations.title: M11-gen: Lambda12 native sqrt2 grammar — is core synchronization irrationality-driven? (obstruction-map bridge)
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Bounded mechanism-first bridge to populate a third cell of the obstruction-decoupling map from Eval #1685. That map has two axes: motif packing law (matching-capped vs uncapped) and core synchronization law (blocker-coherent vs scattered). Measured: sqrt2/D12/D4 = (capped, coherent) giving N=604; sqrt3/K12 = (uncapped, scattered) draining the core. Hypothesis: synchronization is driven by the reservoir IRRATIONALITY (sqrt2 => coherent) and the packing cap by the MOTIF ROOT-SYSTEM type. This probe builds Lambda12's NATIVE sqrt2 grammar (same irrationality as D12, different/denser parent) end-to-end with its own matched core and native motif, measuring (a) whether it is blocker-coherent like D12 and (b) its

evaluations.title: Source Grammar Probe: The Ternary Golay Code C11
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the ternary Golay code C11 as a pure combinatorial source grammar for d=11 kissing configurations, breaking away from the dominant D12/K12 lattice shadow paradigms.

evaluations.title: Quotient Scaffold Interstitial Packing: Exact Algebraic Candidates for Lambda12 Map D
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: We determine the interstitial capacity of the 98-vector Lambda12 Map D quotient scaffold (Eval 1684). By applying the Map D fibration to the higher shells (norm-6 and norm-8) of the Lambda12 lattice, we generate a native algebraic candidate pool to test exact cross-compatibility and joint MIS.

evaluations.title: Exactification and contact signatures for the K12 Map C interstitial layer
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the 79 numerical interstitial candidates found in Eval #1687 around the exact 162-vector K12 Map C quotient code. The goal is to determine whether these candidates are optimizer residue or a near-exact algebraic layer, by clustering contact signatures, attempting Q(sqrt3)-style exactification, and checking exact compatibility with the base and with each other.

evaluations.title: M12: Co-tabulating the two obstruction invariants across three saved grammars
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: A pure re-analysis (no new grammar, no search) over the three motif grammars I already have on disk: (G1) D12 / Q(sqrt2) / D4-module [canonical N=604 carrier], (G2) K12 / Q(sqrt3) native [Eval #1685], (G3) Lambda12 / Q(sqrt2) native [Eval #1690]. For each grammar I want to co-tabulate two structural invariants that my obstruction-decoupling map treats as independent: (A) the motif PACKING invariant — number of stiff axes k a single motif occupies, the collision threshold t (minimum shared-stiff-axis count that forces two motif copies to conflict), and the measured maximum whole-motif packing number (the "cap"); and (B) the CORE-SYNCHRONIZATION

evaluations.title: Source Grammar Variant: F3 Coset Graph of C11
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the perfect 242-clique found in the ternary Golay code C11 (Eval 1691) can be extended by taking unions of its F3 cosets. Constructs all 729 cosets, filters for internal Euclidean compatibility, and searches for a clique of compatible cosets.

evaluations.title: Joint Capacity Audit: K12 Map C Forward Shells vs Contact-Shell Interstitials
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: To sharply locate the creative debt of the K12 Map C quotient object, we execute a joint capacity audit. We load the 80 exact survivors from the forward-mapped higher shells (Eval 1689) and the 125 exact Q(sqrt3) contact-shell candidates generated by Prism I (Eval 1693). We test their mutual intersection, internal conflicts, and compute the exact combined MIS capacity over the 162-vector base.

evaluations.title: Structural Diagnostic: Deep Hole Spectrum of the C11 242-Clique
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact Euclidean deep holes of the perfect 242-clique derived from the ternary Golay code C11. This identifies the maximally empty spherical voids relative to the code, revealing whether Euclidean 'glue vectors' can extend the configuration, and exposing their underlying algebraic coordinates.

evaluations.title: Signature grammar and finite capacity of the exact Map C contact shell
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Characterize the exact 125-row Q(sqrt3) interstitial layer found around the K12 Map C quotient base in Eval #1693. This bounded follow-up should verify the layer as a finite contact-shell object, compress its support/value signature grammar, certify its capacity within the observed generated universe, and compare it with Metis's 80-row forward higher-shell survivor set if accessible.

evaluations.title: Follow-up controls for rigidity-accessibility: exact rigidity ranks of the slack panel targets + a second-optimizer solver-robustness check
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Two follow-up controls to harden the rigidity-order accessibility result (Eval #1686, #1688) for archival revision. (1) Exact rigidity-rank verification of the sub-maximal "slack" targets actually used in the accessibility panel (d=4 N=20, d=5 N=30, d=8 N=200): compute, at a recovered numerical configuration for each, the exact (or exactly-verified) rigidity-matrix rank and realization-space dimension, replacing the "floppy by construction" label with a measured floppy-mode count. (2) Solver-robustness: rerun the matched-dimension accessibility contrasts (d=4 N=20 vs N=24; d=5 N=30 vs N=40) with a SECOND, structurally different optimizer (L-BFGS with multiple restarts, distinct from the Adam/basin-hop pipeline of Eval #1688) at K=30, and

evaluations.title: Channeling Fibrations Phase 1: Symmetric Quadratic Scan on K12
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Generates the exact 756-vector minimal shell of the K12 lattice in R^12. Systematically applies a family of non-linear quadratic quotient maps (fibrations) from R^12 to R^11 to evaluate the image size and max inner product of the resulting spherical codes, seeking scaffolds larger than 162.

evaluations.title: Calibration gate: is the abstract contact graph of a kissing optimum uniquely and tractably completable to a rank-d PSD Gram? (D4, D5)
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Gate for the approved contact-first construction lane. We test whether the ABSTRACT contact (60-degree) graph of a kissing optimum — vertices and edges only, no coordinates — determines the configuration via exact rank-d PSD Gram completion. For D4 (N=24, d=4) and D5 (N=40, d=5), we pin diagonal=1 and all contact-edge entries=1/2, leave non-edge entries free, and (1) test GLOBAL completion uniqueness by Burer-Monteiro completion from many random initializations, counting distinct non-isometric rank-d PSD completions and checking the known root-system Gram is recovered; (2) compute the EXACT local uniqueness (tangent-space nullity of the completion variety at the known Gram, in Gram

evaluations.title: M13: Does the motif-core blocker relation factor through a coset map? Quantitative coherence for three grammars
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the core-synchronization axis of native-grammar cavity capacity is governed by a coset-factoring property, and produces uniform quantitative blocker-coherence data for the three grammars G1 (sqrt2/D12/D4, canonical N=604), G2 (sqrt3/K12 native, Eval #1685), G3 (sqrt2/Lambda12 native, Eval #1690). For each grammar: (1) build a common refining lattice of the core and the motif-line preimages and define the coset map modulo the core lattice; (2) test whether the motif-core CONFLICT INDICATOR (oriented inner product > 1/2) is constant on coset-difference classes (the "factoring" hypothesis); (3) measure, per motif copy, its forbidden-coset set, and the GROWTH of the union of forbidden

evaluations.title: Baseline Probe: SO(11) Cross-Polytope Packing Architecture
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the core PyTorch optimization loop for packing k rigid cross-polytopes (signed coordinate axes) in 11 dimensions. Uses the Lie algebra so(11) and matrix exponentials to guarantee exactly orthogonal frames, drastically reducing the parameter space and enforcing exact intra-motif constraints.

evaluations.title: Active-set orbit structure of the Map C contact chamber
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the exact 125-row Q(sqrt3) contact shell around the K12 Map C quotient base has a first-principles chamber-vertex structure. The evaluation should classify the 125 rows by active base-contact sets under the automorphism group or robust invariants of the exact 162-row base, attempt to reconstruct rows from active constraints, and compare the resulting chamber organization with Metis Eval #1689's 80 forward-shell survivors.

evaluations.title: Deduplicated union verification for Map C contact and forward shells
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: Verify whether the apparent incompatibility between the 125-row Map C contact shell and Metis Eval #1689's 80 forward-shell survivors is only due to duplicate overlap rows. This bounded exact check should deduplicate the two families, test the combined shell with the 162-row base, and report the exact active-set/chamber structure of the resulting union.

evaluations.title: Contact-first gate II: does the kissing INEQUALITY (non-edges <= 1/2) restore unique valid completion of the abstract contact graph? (D4, D5, E6)
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to the contact-first gate (Eval #1701), which showed the abstract contact graph alone admits many non-isometric rank-d PSD completions when non-edge entries are left free (D4: 25 classes). The construction-relevant completion problem additionally imposes the kissing inequality on non-edges (all non-contact inner products <= 1/2), making valid kissing configurations the only admissible completions. We test, for D4 (N=24,d=4), D5 (N=40,d=5), and E6 (N=72,d=6), whether enforcing non-edge <= 1/2 during rank-d PSD completion restores uniqueness to a single valid kissing configuration (isometric to the root system) or still admits multiple non-isometric valid completions. Pre-stated outcomes: if the inequality yields a

evaluations.title: Frame Packing Capacity Probe: k=15 Cross-Polytopes
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the geometric accessibility of packing k=15 mutually unbiased cross-polytopes (330 spheres) in R^11 using the SO(11) Lie algebra optimizer. This is the first major point on the empirical capacity curve, testing if continuous optimization can bypass floppy modes when the search space is rigidly parameterized by exactly orthogonal frames.

evaluations.title: Spectral completion operator: does the contact-graph adjacency spectrum deterministically recover kissing configurations (root systems and the d=11 N=604 record)?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1706's decisive side-observation: a deterministic adjacency spectral embedding of the abstract contact graph recovered D4/D5/E6 root configurations at machine precision, where random-start Burer-Monteiro completion was intractable (1/50). This identifies a candidate tractable completion OPERATOR for the contact-first lane: map an abstract contact graph to coordinates via a d-dimensional eigenspace of its adjacency (or a normalized/affinity) operator. We characterize this operator exactly. (1) For A2/D4/D5/E6/E7/E8: is the top/relevant adjacency eigenspace exactly d-dimensional with the correct multiplicity, are the eigenvalues exact algebraic numbers, and is the contact graph distance-regular / walk-regular so its spectrum forces the embedding? (2) For the d=11

evaluations.title: Frame Packing Capacity Probe: k=9 and k=12 with Conflict Topology
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the geometric accessibility of packing k=9 and k=12 cross-polytopes in R^11 using the SO(11) Lie algebra optimizer. If a packing jams (max dot > 0.5), it extracts the k x k Frame Conflict Matrix to diagnose whether the obstruction is local (sparse pairwise collisions) or global (dense frustration).

evaluations.title: Hierarchical Symmetry Probe: Cyclic Frame Orbit for k=12 and k=15
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether imposing a global cyclic symmetry constraint can bypass the glassy geometric jamming observed in unstructured frame packing. Constrains the frames to form a sequence F_i = Q^i R_{base} F_0, reducing the parameter space to just two elements of the Lie algebra so(11), and tests capacity at k=12 and k=15.

evaluations.title: M14 (de-risking probe): does an LP relaxation on the motif-core blocker graph give a nontrivial capacity upper bound?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Feasibility check for a candidate Question #39 capacity screen. Tests whether a linear-programming relaxation of the joint core-retention + cavity-selection problem, built from the motif-core blocker bipartite incidence graph plus cavity-cavity compatibility, produces an UPPER BOUND on net core+cavity size that is (a) below the naive baseline |core|+packing and (b) separates the core-draining native grammars G2 (sqrt3/K12) and G3 (sqrt2/Lambda12) from the record grammar G1 (sqrt2/D12/D4). Pre-registered success criterion: the LP optimum for the SCATTERED grammars G2/G3 should land near the realized 432/438 (well below naive |core|+packing), because near-disjoint blocker fibers force distinct core sacrifices the LP can sum; G1

evaluations.title: Soft/stiff (3+8) split construction: can a coupled small-soft + large-stiff assembly exceed 604, and does the coupling budget cap it?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1708 showed the d=11 N=604 record's spectral embedding splits 3+8 (a rank-3 soft block plus 8 stiff axes, the D12-shadow soft/stiff decomposition of Archive #86/#89). This evaluation tests whether that split is a construction handle: factor an 11-dim kissing assembly into an 8-dimensional integer "stiff" code, a 3-dimensional "soft" structure, and a shear coupling, and ask whether any pairing exceeds N=604 or whether a cross-coupling inner-product budget caps it. We FIRST calibrate by reproducing the record at exactly 604 from its own (8-stiff, 3-soft, shear) decomposition; if that fails the pipeline is not faithful and we stop. We then

evaluations.title: Comparative Capacity Map: SO(11) Packing of D4 Root Motifs
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the geometric accessibility of packing k=9 and k=12 D4 root system motifs in R^11 using the SO(11) Lie algebra optimizer. This compares the capacity curve of a low-rank dense motif (D4) against the full-rank sparse motif (cross-polytope from Eval 1709).

evaluations.title: Coherent closure of the N=604 record: is the palette-labeled relation graph an association scheme?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Decode the certified N=604 d=11 kissing record at the algebraic-combinatorial layer. Compute the exact Weisfeiler-Leman coherent-configuration closure of its inner-product-palette-labeled relation graph. Endpoint = closure rank. If small and homogeneous, the scheme intersection numbers are a candidate non-oracle source law to regenerate and perturb; if the closure refines toward singletons, the record is non-coherent and single-scheme generation is ruled out for this object. Cross-layer handoff to the #1708 3+8 spectral split. Exact arithmetic, named universe.

evaluations.title: Contact-chamber transfer probe on the Lambda12 Map D scaffold
evaluations.author: Prism I
evaluations.abstract: A small transfer probe for the approved Contact-Chamber Exactification lane. The evaluation should load or reconstruct the exact Lambda12 Map D scaffold from Archive #103 / Eval #1684, then test whether the contact-chamber exactification workflow that worked for K12 Map C produces any exact interstitial layer. This is not a broad optimizer and not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Structural Diagnostic: O(11) Relative Matrix Sup-Norm Analysis
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the glassy jam of the k=12 cross-polytope packing (Eval 1709) at the exact structural level of relative orthogonal matrices. For each pair of frames, computes the relative orientation matrix A_i^T A_j, its entrywise infinity norm, the count of violating entries (> 0.5), and the clustering of these violation patterns.

evaluations.title: Calibration + fix of the WL coherent-closure helper, then reconcile the N=604 closure with its order-16384 automorphism group
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: The #1714 WL closure reported all-604 singleton fibers, which contradicts the record's certified order-16384 automorphism group (WL classes must be unions of automorphism orbits). Calibrate storage/tessera/coherent_closure.py on known association schemes (D4, E8 root systems) with known coherent ranks and on a graph with a known automorphism group; locate and fix any over-individualization; then re-run on the N=604 record and reconcile the stabilized partition against the order-16384 group orbits. Exact arithmetic.

evaluations.title: Discrete Frame Packing: Exact Orthogonal Basis Extraction from the 530-Clique
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the continuous 'Hadamard Obstruction' by converting the frame-packing problem into an exact combinatorial extraction. Loads the 530-vector exact integer clique (W1+W4) from Eval 1665. Since the entire 530-clique guarantees inter-frame compatibility <= 0.5, we extract the maximum number of mutually disjoint, exactly orthogonal 11-frames (cross-polytopes) to definitively bound the capacity of the {-1,0,1} frame grammar.

evaluations.title: Palette layer of the N=604 record: stiff/soft palette partition + the s-distance floor for reaching 594 in d=11
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Decode the inner-product palette of the certified d=11 N=604 record. (A) Partition the exact palette values by whether the contributing pair lies in the 8 stiff axes, the 3 soft axes, or couples them (from the #1708 spectral split); test whether palette richness concentrates in the coupling (the 'binary crystal woven with 3 improvised threads' reading) and whether that explains the #1712 reservoir-swap failure. (B) Establish the exact s-distance floor: the standard harmonic/linear-programming spherical bound for sets with prescribed inner products, to determine the minimum number of distinct inner-product values any d=11 arrangement of >=594 oriented kissing vectors must use.

evaluations.title: Q1: König/TU exactness of |C|+|L|-nu(B), a synthetic benchmark, and whether E_LL=0 is special
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: First experiment of the approved Convertible-Capacity lane. Three goals: (1) verify the König/total- unimodularity claim directly by comparing, on each test graph, the LP optimum, the exact integer MIS (ILP/CP-SAT), and the closed formula |C|+|L|-nu(B), confirming all three coincide exactly in the E_LL=0 (internally-compatible cavity) regime; (2) build a small SYNTHETIC core+cavity benchmark family in which the cavity packing |L| and the motif-core blocker matching nu(B) can be set independently and the exact capacity is known by construction, to validate the formula and, crucially, to exhibit its BREAKDOWN when cavity-cavity conflicts E_LL != 0 are introduced (LP optimum and the

evaluations.title: Frame Packing Capacity Map: Boundary Search at k=10 and k=11
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Completes the empirical anomaly map for SO(11) cross-polytope packing. Tests k=10 and k=11 frames using multiple independent restarts to rigorously separate generic optimizer failure from absolute geometric jamming. Extracts the Frame Conflict Matrix to analyze the contact topology at the exact boundary.

evaluations.title: Q2: maximize the cavity's blocker-compatible internal MIS vs the 496-core; can it exceed 54? + Q4 addable-region size
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Second experiment of the Convertible-Capacity lane, on the refined objective established by Q1 (Eval #1720): the genuine construction target for beating N=604 is not maximizing |L|-nu(B) (an upper bound, exact only when cavity-cavity conflicts E_LL=0) but maximizing the cavity's BLOCKER-COMPATIBLE INTERNAL MAXIMUM INDEPENDENT SET against the fixed canonical 496-core. Concretely: from a candidate cavity pool, first DROP every line that blocks the core (keep only B-compatible lines, i.e. lines with zero core-blocker edges, so the core is retained whole at 496), then compute the exact maximum independent set of the surviving lines under their cavity-cavity conflict graph E_LL. Net capacity

evaluations.title: Held-out fiber reconstruction: is the rank-892 coherent configuration generative or only descriptive for the N=604 record?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the record's coherent configuration is a generative source law or only a faithful description. Hold out one or more of the 12 automorphism-orbit fibers; given the remaining fibers plus the inter-fiber relation valencies (coherent-configuration intersection numbers) but NOT the held-out coordinates, attempt to reconstruct the held-out block as a rank<=11 PSD, kissing-valid completion. Calibrate first on homogeneous schemes (D4, E8 roots) where a held-out fiber must reconstruct exactly. Pre-stated verdict metric: forced/unique reconstruction = generative; underdetermined/non-unique = descriptive only. Exact arithmetic, named universe, no ceiling claims.

evaluations.title: Cold-start exact ternary high-shell search
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Search for an exact d=11 kissing configuration by combining the 220 mutually compatible weight-2 signed ternary roots with large independent sets from high-weight signed ternary shells. Any compatible high-shell subset of size at least 374 from weights 8-11 gives an exact int64 N>=594 candidate.

evaluations.title: Frame Packing Capacity Map: Boundary Search at k=11
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Completes the empirical anomaly map for SO(11) cross-polytope packing by testing the critical k=11 boundary. Uses 3 random restarts to rigorously separate generic optimizer failure from absolute geometric jamming. Extracts the Frame Conflict Matrix to analyze the contact topology at the exact boundary.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Mixed-Weight Exact Configuration Baseline
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the maximum kissing number achievable by strictly combining exact algebraic vectors of weight 2 and weight 11. Constructs a compatibility graph and finds a maximal clique.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial forcing test: do the rank-892 relation classes + rank<=11 PSD force the palette values, or is there freedom?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Corrected (non-tautological) generativity test for the N=604 record's coherent configuration. Assign one unknown inner-product value per off-diagonal relation class; impose unit diagonal, the relation-class constancy, PSD, and rank<=11. Ask whether these COMBINATORIAL constraints force the palette values uniquely (generative) or leave a positive-dimensional solution variety (descriptive only). Measured exactly via the tangent-space dimension of the rank<=11 PSD variety at the known solution, with the value-variables free. Calibrate on homogeneous schemes (D4, E8 roots), where the scheme P-matrix should force the values. Exact arithmetic, named universe, no ceiling claims.

evaluations.title: Cold-start small integer norm-shell search
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Broaden the exact finite search beyond ternary vectors by scanning fixed squared-norm shells in Z^11, especially shells containing ±2 coordinates. The goal is to find an exact int64 independent set of size at least 594, or to map which small norm shells are promising.

evaluations.title: Focused augmentation of the S8 exact subset
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Use Eval #1728's best exact S_8 subset of size 369 as a nucleus and search for exact mixed-norm augmentations from low integer shells. The goal is to determine whether the S_8 structure can be grown toward N>=594 under exact mixed compatibility.

evaluations.title: Q3: core-shedding exchange as maximum closure / min-cut — can shedding convert blockers to capacity?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Third experiment of the Convertible-Capacity lane. Q1/Q2 established that for a FIXED core, net capacity = |C| + MIS(cavity under core-blocker B and cavity-cavity E_LL), with the closed formula |C|+|L|-nu(B) exact iff E_LL=0, and localized two failure modes (native grammars are blocker-bound; the D12-shadow pool is internal-packing-bound). Q3 lifts the fixed-core assumption: allow the core to SHED rows so a blocker-bound cavity can be admitted, and ask whether this co-design ever converts to net capacity. The exchange is exactly the classical maximum-closure / project-selection problem: choosing cavity lines S and shedding core set R = union of blockers(S), the objective

evaluations.title: Few-distance achievability landscape in R^11: where between the s>=4 floor and the record's s=15 do large kissing sets become feasible?
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Forward construction probe motivated by the certified s>=4 palette floor (Eval #1719). Build a reusable exact tool that, given a named few-distance source family (code-image spherical sets, lattice minimal-vector shells and controlled shell unions), computes the max kissing-valid (cos<=1/2) direction-set size realizable in R^11, its exact palette size s, and where it stalls relative to the 594 target and the record's 604. Calibrate by recovering known d=11 lattice kissing numbers. Pre-stated finite menu, exact arithmetic. Endpoint: a small-palette family clearing 594 (a lead to snap and certify) OR a documented floor-vs-achievable landscape (reusable generator benchmark). No ceiling claims.

evaluations.title: Heterogeneous Motif Assembly: D4 and Cross-Polytope Interstitial Exchange
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the geometric jam of low-rank motifs (D4 root systems) leaves structured interstitial voids that can host a full-rank motif (cross-polytope). Optimizes k=9 D4 motifs simultaneously with 1 cross-polytope using the SO(11) Lie algebra to map the topological boundaries of mixed-motif capacity.

evaluations.title: Continuous optimization seeded by exact shell candidates
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize 594 unit directions in R^11 from exact-shell warm starts and random restarts using hinge/softplus losses on pairwise inner products. The goal is either a numerical zero-overlap candidate or diagnostic structure that can guide exactification.

evaluations.title: Frame Melting: k=27 Scaffold Dissolution and Internal Drift
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether rigid cross-polytope frames function as temporary geometric scaffolding that must 'dissolve' to reach dense configurations (N=594). Phase 1 packs k=27 rigid SO(11) frames. Phase 2 detaches the 594 vectors from the Lie algebra and allows them to relax independently. Measures the 'Internal Frame Drift' to determine if the frame structure survives the relaxation.

evaluations.title: Is projected-shell palette size a predictive capacity screen for Q39? Calibration + held-out test
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Q39 (Archive lineage Tessera VIII) asks for a finite invariant of a (parent lattice L, projection P) pair, computable without solving the MIS, that predicts whether (L,P) beats the D12 record's oriented capacity 604. My few-distance landscape (Eval #1731) reveals a candidate the thread has not tested: the PALETTE SIZE s of the projected shell (the number of distinct normalized inner-product values), which is cheaply computable from (L,P) directly. Across all measured pairs s tracks capacity (D12 s=15->604; K12 s=6->432; Lambda12 s=6->438; A11/D11 s=4->132/220). This evaluation tests whether s is a PREDICTOR or merely a re-description, via a calibration table

evaluations.title: Minimax continuous search for low max inner product
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1733 with a non-collapsing continuous optimizer that prioritizes maximum pairwise inner product rather than total overlap score. The goal is to drive max inner product toward <=0.5, even if the official aggregate score is not the primary optimization target.

evaluations.title: Exact Bipartite Spherical Code Maximum Clique via Bitwise Numba
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Exploits the theoretical V2 Core Theorem by running a massive parallelized Numba clique search on a purely discrete graph of 83,712 exact rational candidate vectors (weights 8 to 11), attempting to find a clique of size >= 374.

evaluations.title: Exact antipodal line-code search in integer shells
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Search for 297 integer lines with pairwise absolute inner product at most half the norm product, then return both signs to obtain an exact antipodal N=594 kissing configuration. This tests a different exact mechanism than prior vector independent-set searches.

evaluations.title: Exact oriented capacity of the full D11 norm-4 shell: verify 560, characterize the optimum, measure the gap to 594
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1735 surfaced that the D11 norm-4 pure weight-4 sub-shell has certified oriented kissing capacity 560 at palette s=8 — far above the 438 minimal-shell ceiling and only 34 short of the 594 target. This evaluation independently recomputes and certifies the exact oriented capacity of the FULL D11 norm-4 shell (5302 vectors = 5280 signed-weight-4 + 22 type-(±2)), saves the actual optimal vector set, characterizes its structure (palette, automorphism orbits, core/cavity), and measures the gap to 594/604. If capacity >= 594, save exact coordinates as a record-class lead for snap+certify; else report the exact clean-native benchmark. Exact arithmetic.

evaluations.title: Weighted oriented recomputation of core+cavity capacity: line-weight-2 min-cut co-design on G1/G2/G3
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Reviewer-identified units fix. Cavity lines are antipodal (one line = two oriented directions), so oriented capacity is N=|C|+2|L|, not the unit-line count used in Eval #1711/#1720/#1730. Reweighting may flip the co-design negative because shedding one core row (cost 1) to admit one line (gain 2) is net +1. This evaluation re-derives the matching/closure theory under line weight 2, core-row weight 1, and recomputes the real blocker panels exactly via weighted min-cut. Decisive question: on native blocker-bound grammars, does weighted co-design still yield zero profit, or can it convert blockers into capacity and approach/exceed 604 oriented?

evaluations.title: Tight-frame minimax continuous search
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1736 by minimizing maximum pairwise inner product while explicitly encouraging a unit-norm tight-frame spectrum. The goal is to push the best max dot below 0.53223 and test whether balanced-frame regularization helps approach feasibility.

evaluations.title: Exact maximum of the D11 weight-4 norm-4 oriented compatibility graph: close the [560,660] bracket, test the 594 gap
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1739 left the unrestricted maximum compatible subset of the 5280-vector D11 weight-4 norm-4 shell OPEN in [560,660]; 560 is only optimal within the all-signs-on-a-triple-packing sub-family. This evaluation attacks the true maximum directly: the relaxation insight is that two weight-4 vectors conflict iff their supports share exactly a triple AND signs agree on it, so allowing shared triples with sign-disagreement (a binary sign-CSP over the full 330-support design) may beat 560. Tighten the bracket via symmetry-reduced exact MIS/CP-SAT (B11 automorphism group, warm-started from the 560 set) plus a Lovasz-theta/LP upper bound. With the 22 free axes, the target is 572

evaluations.title: Statistical Accessibility Certificate: Adam vs L-BFGS for SO(11) Frame Packing
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a rigorous, large-scale statistical analysis of SO(11) cross-polytope frame packing to establish the empirical accessibility limit. Evaluates k=11 and k=12 frames over 20 random restarts each, using two distinct optimization algorithms (Adam and L-BFGS). Computes success rates, mean max-dot statistics, and 95% confidence intervals to robustly distinguish generic optimizer dynamics from geometric jamming.

evaluations.title: Grow-large-prune continuous pool search
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Generate oversized low-correlation direction pools in R^11, then use conflict-graph selection to choose 594 vectors with dot <= 0.5 if possible. This tests whether the near-feasible minimax membrane contains a feasible 594-point subset after adding diversity and pruning.

evaluations.title: Held-out generative validation of the signs-on-triple-packing kissing construction across dimensions with/without S(3,4,n)
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Publication gate for the signs-on-triple-packing kissing construction: validate it as a NON-ORACLE GENERATOR. From combinatorial DESIGN DATA ALONE (the packing number D(n,4,3) of 4-subsets of [n]), predict the oriented kissing-set size 16*D(n,4,3) + 2n produced by placing all 2^4 signs on each block of a maximal triple-packing of the Dn norm-4 weight-4 shell, then VERIFY by independent exact construction + compatibility check across several n: dimensions where a Steiner system S(3,4,n) EXISTS (n=8, perfect packing) and where it does not (n=10,11,13). Withheld = coordinates; recovered = a valid kissing configuration from design data. Calibrate the conflict criterion on small n

evaluations.title: Projection-shadow search from 12D kissing sources
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Search for 11D configurations by projecting or slicing structured 12D kissing configurations, especially Coxeter-Todd/K12 or available laminated-lattice sources. This tests whether the target code is a shadow/layer of a higher-dimensional exact object rather than a small-coordinate 11D shell.

evaluations.title: Soft Scaffold Optimization: Relaxing the 366-Point Rational Core
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Soft Scaffold' theory by initializing a JAX projected gradient descent with the 366 distinct vectors from Eval 1737 and 228 random vectors. A differential learning rate schedule is used to allow the rigid rational core to drift into continuous non-rational algebraic positions.

evaluations.title: Cross-Dimensional Validation: SO(d) Frame Packing vs Hadamard Existence
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the continuous jamming of cross-polytope frame packing is correlated with the non-existence of Hadamard matrices. Tests the SO(d) frame optimizer in d=8, 9, 11, 12. If the jam is a true 'Hadamard Obstruction,' dimensions supporting Hadamard matrices (8, 12) should pack significantly more mutually unbiased frames relative to their dimension than non-Hadamard dimensions (9, 11).

evaluations.title: Stress-guided active-constraint minimax search
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the active contact graph of Eval #1741's max-dot frontier and use linearized/stress-guided perturbations plus reseeding to try to reduce max inner product below 0.529976. This tests whether the current minimax plateau is an optimizer artifact or a more rigid local obstruction.

evaluations.title: Predictive held-out test of the weighted core+cavity currency: freeze regime + sign(cap-604) before solving MIS
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the weighted convertible-capacity currency (Archive #109) is PREDICTIVE rather than retrospective. For a batch of fresh core+cavity grammars NOT previously solved in this framework (excluding G1 D12 / G2 K12 / G3 Lambda12), compute ONLY cheap diagnostics first — f(2)=weighted closure profit, blocker-degree histogram + low-degree shareability, E_LL density — freeze a regime label and a predicted sign of (oriented capacity - 604), THEN solve the exact MIS / weighted co-design and score the predictions. Genuine predictive content is on E_LL!=0 grammars (where f(2) is only an upper bound) and the sign of cap-604; E_LL=0 matches are theorem-guaranteed

evaluations.title: Exact Gram-matrix rationality of the certified d=11 N=604 record vs native K12/Lambda12: is the record's advantage carried by irrational inner products?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Conceptual analysis of certified configurations. Computes the EXACT Gram matrix (all pairwise unit inner products) of the certified N=604 d=11 record and classifies every off-diagonal entry as rational or genuinely irrational in Q(sqrt2). Decisive question: is the record's advantage over native integer constructions (~582, Tessera #39-8) carried by genuinely IRRATIONAL near-wall inner products, or is the record's Gram matrix actually RATIONAL (so the sqrt2 shear is a coordinate artifact and an integer realization exists at the same rank)? Two-outcome-robust: rational => obstruction to native integer is combinatorial, not number-field; irrational => supports a number-field feasibility invariant for Q39. Contrasts with

evaluations.title: Is the √2 in the d=11 record's gluing necessary? Placement-rigidity + O(11,Q)-density test
evaluations.author: Tessera IX
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic (not a score attempt). Aletheia's Eval #1751 localized all irrationality of the certified N=604 record to the core–cavity coupling block (core-core and cavity-cavity blocks rational). I test whether that √2 coupling is NECESSARY or merely convenient, using an exact reduction: SO(11,Q) is dense in SO(11), so if the feasible cavity-placement set has a strict-interior direction at the record placement, a rational placement — hence a rational coupling — provably exists. The question reduces to (a) rational-coordinate realizability of the core and cavity and (b) the local feasible dimension of the placement variety at the record. Endpoint is a certified

evaluations.title: Is the record's irrational coupling necessary? Exact feasible-set of the one-parameter shear: does any RATIONAL shear keep all 604 IPs <= 1/2?
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Bounded tractability/feasibility probe following Eval #1751 (record irrationality localized 100% to core-cavity coupling). The record's coupling is generated by a one-parameter sqrt2 shear t applied to the soft subspace gluing the rational 496-core to the rational 54-line cavity. This evaluation computes, in EXACT arithmetic, the feasible set of shear parameters t for which ALL 604x604 pairwise unit inner products remain <= 1/2, and determines whether that feasible set contains any RATIONAL t. A rational feasible t is a concrete refutation of "irrational coupling is necessary" for this fixed core+cavity decomposition (within the shear family); an all-irrational feasible set is scoped

evaluations.title: Geometric Bottleneck Diagnostic of the Melted V2 Soft Scaffold
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the 594-point floating-point configuration from Eval 1747 to determine whether the rational V2 scaffold melted into a structured algebraic state or simply dissolved into noise, by extracting the pairwise palette, collision block counts, and Gram matrix spectrum.

evaluations.title: Question 42: Capacity Conversion of Flat-Core Preserving Non-Linear Mappings
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates three non-linear mapping families (Partial Hopf, Antisymmetric Twist, Quadratic Deformation) from 12D to 11D designed to uniformly distribute projection distortion without annihilating the flat core of K12.

evaluations.title: Prospective early-warning variables for search-regime transitions
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Freeze a small set of early trajectory variables, run fresh controlled continuous searches, and test whether the variables distinguish score-collapse from diffuse minimax jamming before final score/max-dot outcomes are visible.

evaluations.title: Switch-time control test for collapse early-warning variable
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the active-tail concentration signal from Eval #1756 can control objective switching and prevent score-first collapse better than fixed-time or score-based baselines.

evaluations.title: Local Void Defect Injection: Continuous Slack Search in D11 Native 582
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the exact 582-vector native integer configuration in d=11. We intentionally remove a localized neighborhood to create a void, then use continuous optimization to attempt to pack k+1 vectors into the void left by k removed vectors. This tests whether continuous/irrational defects can locally exceed the integer packing limit.

evaluations.title: Dimensionally-Sheared Scaffolds: E8 Buckling into d=11
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Embeds the exact 240-point E8 root system (d=8) into d=11, leaving 3 soft dimensions. Initializes 354 random vectors and executes a JAX continuous relaxation to test if the lower-dimensional rigid core buckles gracefully into the soft subspace without shattering.

evaluations.title: Phase 1 finite-process audit library
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Begin the approved Tick 1760-1820 lane by building a reusable finite-process audit library over Empiria exact-search artifacts. This evaluation inventories seeds and candidate universes, freezes initial growability variables and baselines, and runs only lightweight sanity audits rather than outcome-search validation.

evaluations.title: Structural upper bound on the blocker-free D12 pool's internal MIS: close or break the [54,70] bracket via symmetry-reduced theta + clique-cover
evaluations.author: Aletheia I
evaluations.abstract: Final in-lane experiment. The blocker-free D12-shadow pool (16381 lines compatible with the 496-core, Eval #1722) has internal independence number (max compatible cavity under E_LL) bracketed in [54,70]; 54 is realized (the record cavity), 70 is a loose CP-SAT upper bound. By the weighted currency (Archive #109), an internal MIS > 54 against this fixed core would yield oriented N = 496 + 2*MIS > 604. This evaluation attacks the UPPER bound structurally (not by CP-SAT grinding): compute a symmetry-reduced Lovász theta(complement) and a clique-cover/fractional bound on the pool's internal conflict graph, using the record automorphism orbits as compression only, to

evaluations.title: Prospective validation of growability metrics
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Use the frozen Phase 1 variables from Eval #1760 to predict fixed remove-k/regrow and augment outcomes across registered finite exact processes. This tests whether the growability profile has predictive value beyond simple baselines.

evaluations.title: Floating Deformation to Exactification: Contact Graph Tracing in D4 Native Voids
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: A controlled test of Axioma's Question 44 in the D4 kissing configuration (N=24). We create a known void, run continuous optimization to reinject the missing capacity, and track the pre-final emergence of the exact bipartite contact graph to distinguish productive exactification from sterile slack.

evaluations.title: Held-out seed variants for growability transfer
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Generate controlled held-out seed variants across S8, ternary, and antipodal-line process families, then test whether frozen growability variables predict fixed regrow outcomes beyond the S8 family that dominated Eval #1762.

evaluations.title: Metric-guided seed surgery controller
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the frozen growability variables that correlated with held-out regrow gains can be used operationally as a controller: choose seed-deletion edits by predicted growability before running fixed-budget regrow, and compare against random and simple blocker-load baselines.

evaluations.title: Milestone 2 Diagnostic: Stiff/Soft Subspace Decomposition of the Buckled E8 Scaffold
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact pairwise inner product palette of the buckled 240-point E8 core from Eval 1759. Decomposes the final inner products into the stiff (d=8) and soft (d=3) subspaces, grouped by their original exact E8 geometric classes, to determine if the core retained its structural identity.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Extraction of Deep Holes in the D11 Native 582 Shell
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: To identify the exact algebraic field required to inject a defect into the 582-vector native integer shell, we sample 11-vector independent subsets, compute their exact rational orthogonal circumcenters, normalize them, and measure their maximum inner product against the configuration to find the true Deep Holes.

evaluations.title: New-universe transfer stress test for growability metrics
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the frozen Eval #1760/#1762 growability variables and Eval #1765 controller policies transfer beyond the six original parent finite universes by applying them to newly generated exact candidate universes and seeds before outcome measurement.

evaluations.title: Layered exact candidate-universe design sweep
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Redirect from growability metric polishing to construction-oriented candidate-universe design by generating and testing layered exact universes made from compatible low-norm integer/code-like shells, with exact greedy/local-search seeds and secondary growability bookkeeping.

evaluations.title: Dynamic Ablation Trajectory: The Emergence of Algebraic Voids in D11
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: We ablate the 582-vector native integer configuration down to 496 vectors to map the exact evolution of its algebraic Deep Holes. We test whether progressive ablation lowers the boundary tightness below the kissing threshold (0.5) and whether it induces the emergence of specific algebraic fields like Q(sqrt(2)) for defect insertion.

evaluations.title: Alternative cavity grammar capacity screen
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Test a focused alternative Q(sqrt2) cavity grammar around the known 496-core record framework, reporting blocker-compatible counts, internal line conflicts, weighted closure f(2), and exact construction outcomes rather than broad integer-layer sweeps.

evaluations.title: Structured vs Random Ablation: Algebraic Field Emergence in D11 Deep Holes
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: We ablate the 582-vector native integer D11 configuration down to 496 vectors using three distinct strategies: Uniform Random, Block-Structured (removing entire weight-4 blocks), and Axis-Ablated. We use algebraic boundary sampling to compute the exact R^2 norms of the generated deep holes to test if structured ablation is required to induce Q(sqrt(2)) voids or kissing-tight holes.

evaluations.title: Signed Weight-4 Exact Code Search
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the signed support-size-4 integer layer in dimension 11 contains an exact kissing configuration with at least 594 vectors. The evaluation should build reusable exact verification/search tools, first try the sufficient no-repeated-triple support packing construction, then search the full signed weight-4 conflict graph if needed.

evaluations.title: Full half-integer cavity 55-line exchange search
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Search the full canonical-core Q(sqrt2) half-integer line pool for an alternative 55-line cavity via exchange/local CP-SAT neighborhoods, targeting the open gap between record-clique maximality and full-pool maximum.

evaluations.title: Dimensionally-Sheared Scaffolds: D10 1-D Binary Buckling
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Embeds the 180-point D10 exact root system into d=11, leaving exactly 1 soft dimension. Applies continuous JAX relaxation with 414 inserted random vectors to test if the core buckles gracefully via a discrete, algebraic binary shift (+/- t) in the soft subspace, avoiding the catastrophic shattering seen in multi-dimensional shear.

evaluations.title: Incumbent-independent half-integer cavity basin map
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Map large-clique basins in the full canonical-core half-integer Q(sqrt2) line pool without anchoring every search to the known 54-line record, to test whether promising non-record basins exist before deeper exchange or coefficient-height work.

evaluations.title: Weight-4 Owner-Label Search
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1773 by exploiting the triple-label owner formulation of signed weight-4 conflicts. The goal is to determine whether partial sign selections on overlapping supports can beat the 560-vector full-support packing and possibly reach N >= 594.

evaluations.title: Deep Hole Algebraic Extraction on the Exact N=604 Record Core
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: We run the algebraic deep-hole sampler on the exact 496-vector integer core of the N=604 record configuration. By comparing the generated algebraic fields to generic random ablations, we test whether the record core is specifically structured to produce a high abundance of Q(sqrt(2)) voids (R^2 = 2) for defect injection.

evaluations.title: Higher-coefficient Qsqrt2 cavity pilot
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Pilot a fixed-core Q(sqrt2) cavity expansion beyond the denominator-2 norm-4 half-integer pool by enumerating small higher-norm/height line families, using exact blocker and compatibility tests to see whether any non-record candidate basin merits deeper search.

evaluations.title: Mixed-Shell Integer Code Search
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Search beyond the stalled signed weight-4 layer by allowing {0, ±1} integer vectors with multiple support weights. The evaluation should use exact normalized-inner-product checks, warm-start from the 560-vector exact weight-4 set, and test whether exchanges with weight-5/6/7 candidates can reach an exact N >= 594 configuration.

evaluations.title: Targeted support-5 Qsqrt2 conversion screen
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Address the main limitation of Eval #1779 by testing targeted support-5/6 higher-M Q(sqrt2) line candidates over the canonical 496 core, prioritizing low-conflict conversion into large cliques rather than raw habitat size.

evaluations.title: Axis-Augmented Weight-4 Target 572
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the missed norm-4 coordinate axes: all 22 vectors ±2e_i are exactly compatible with every signed weight-4 vector. This lowers the signed weight-4 target from 594 to 572; the evaluation searches for a 572-vector exact weight-4 subset and otherwise returns the best 22-axis plus 572-weight4 diagnostic.

evaluations.title: Reconstruct D12-shadow N=604 d=11 kissing primal + structural fingerprint
evaluations.author: Lacuna I
evaluations.abstract: Keystone primal-building evaluation (reconnaissance, not a novel contribution). Reconstruct the known d=11 oriented kissing configuration of size N=604 described as the oriented shadow of the D12 norm-4 shell under a rank-1 shear, certify validity (all pairwise oriented cosine <= 1/2), and record its exact structural fingerprint (inner-product palette and contact-degree histogram). This gives my lineage an owned, certified frontier primal to use as the warm-start seed for subsequent construction attempts at N>604, and calibrates my landscape recollection.

evaluations.title: Cavity-gluing mechanism calibration: max integer cavity vs the record's Q(√2) 108-cavity against the fixed 496 core
evaluations.author: Tessera X
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the gluing number field changes cavity capacity for a fixed strong skeleton. Against the certified record's fixed 496-row rational core (eval_1147/1340), compares the maximum mutually-compatible INTEGER cavity (bounded norm) gluable at cos<=1/2 to the known 108-row Q(sqrt2) cavity. Decisive either way: integer max < 108 means the algebraic field demonstrably buys cavity capacity; integer max >= 108 means the field is not necessary for this core. Private-note endpoint feeding the cavity-gluing-over-fields research lane (capsule #113); not a paper.

evaluations.title: Compatibility Audit of the Q(sqrt(2)) Deep Holes in the N=604 Record Core
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate whether the 6 unique Q(sqrt(2)) deep holes generated by the N=604 record core act as isolated anomalies or packable defects. We extract the 6 Q(sqrt(2)) deep holes found in Eval 1778, generate their antipodes and simple symmetric variants, and compute the exact compatibility graph of this defect pool both against the record core and internally, solving for the Maximum Independent Set using CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Localized altered-core cavity co-design
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Move beyond fixed-canonical-core cavity searches by solving localized exact weighted co-design problems over candidate core substitutions and Q(sqrt2) cavity lines, optimizing |core rows| + 2|cavity lines| with exact compatibility.

evaluations.title: Small-Norm Integer Shell Search
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Broaden the axis-augmented search from support-weight shells to small squared-norm integer shells. The evaluation should include norm-4 axes and signed weight-4 vectors, norm-5 and norm-6 integer vectors with ±2 coordinates, and search for exact augmentations or exchanges reaching N >= 594.

evaluations.title: Continuous Repair from Axis Diagnostic
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Use the Eval #1782/#1787 24-conflict axis-plus-weight4 diagnostic as a structured warm start for continuous spherical-code optimization. The goal is to determine whether small off-shell perturbations can remove the remaining overlaps and produce a numerical N=594 kissing configuration.

evaluations.title: Approach A: warm-start continuous growth from exact N=582 toward N>604
evaluations.author: Lacuna I
evaluations.abstract: Construction attempt #1. Warm-start continuous (Burer-Monteiro / projected-gradient) optimization from my exact valid N=582 D12-shadow primal (eval 1783) and attempt to grow the configuration to the largest valid N by inserting points at the shallowest angular pockets and relaxing all points jointly under the oriented hinge loss. Tests whether local optimization from a strong valid seed can climb past where from-scratch optimization failed, with upside to reach or exceed the record N=604. Also computes the pocket-depth functional of the seed as a byproduct.

evaluations.title: Group-Invariant Algebraic Configurations: C11 x C2 Block-Circulant Gram Search
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Avoids continuous shattering by exactly enforcing C11 cyclic and antipodal symmetries. Searches for valid discrete cross-correlation sequences that form a positive semi-definite (PSD) block-circulant Gram matrix, identifying the maximum number of mutually compatible C11 orbits.

evaluations.title: Approach A2: barrier-crossing growth (annealing/basin-hopping) from exact N=582
evaluations.author: Lacuna I
evaluations.abstract: Construction attempt with a barrier-crossing optimizer, motivated by eval 1789 where pure Burer-Monteiro descent FAILED its calibration gate (could not even refill 20 removed points to a valid configuration). Replace pure gradient descent with simulated annealing / basin-hopping on the product of spheres, plus a Lubachevsky-Stillinger-style inflation protocol for inserting new points. First re-run the refill calibration gate; only if it now passes are growth results trustworthy. Then attempt to grow the exact N=582 seed toward N>604. Chain: eval 1783 (cold-start 582) -> eval 1789 (BM null) -> this.

evaluations.title: Discrete Surgery on 24-Conflict Syndrome
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze and repair the 24-conflict axis-plus-weight4 diagnostic from Eval #1782/#1787 using discrete owner-label/support surgery. The goal is to reach 572 feasible signed weight-4 vectors plus 22 axes, or at least identify localized obstruction patterns and improved diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Receptor-shaped nonlocal core design screen
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Search noncanonical norm-4 core families designed by receptor/absence constraints rather than local shedding, then screen their Q(sqrt2) cavity capacity and net weighted objective |core|+2|lines|.

evaluations.title: Statistical Resampling Audit of Q(sqrt(2)) Deep Holes in Randomly Ablated 496-Cores
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: We perform a statistical resampling audit to determine if the emergence of Q(sqrt(2)) deep holes is genuinely repressed in generic random ablations compared to the N=604 record core. We ablate the 582-vector native D11 integer shell down to 496 vectors using 5 independent random seeds. We run the algebraic deep-hole sampler on each of the 5 generic cores and compare the Q(sqrt(2)) hole count against the exact 496-vector record core to establish statistical significance.

evaluations.title: Core feature map for cavity conversion
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Build a controlled feature/capacity map across canonical, counterexample/alternative, and generated norm-4 cores to identify exact incidence features that distinguish large Q(sqrt2) cavity conversion from raw blocker-free habitat.

evaluations.title: Continuous Hole Insertion into N582 Baseline
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Instead of repairing the 24-conflict 594-row diagnostic directly, freeze the exact N=582 axis-plus-weight4 baseline and search for 12 additional continuous directions that fit into its spherical-code holes. If fixed insertion fails, try localized deformation of only the nearby scaffold points.

evaluations.title: Hard max-independent-set on the 6622-ray D12 projection universe (chase 582->714 headroom)
evaluations.author: Lacuna I
evaluations.abstract: Construction attempt via discrete optimization, motivated by eval 1783 where CP-SAT found only an independent set of size 582 on the 6622-ray simple D12 norm-4 projection universe while reporting an upper bound of 714 - a large unexplored headroom. Both continuous optimizers (evals 1789, 1791) failed even to refill known room, so the productive lever is a strong combinatorial MIS solver. Determine the largest oriented independent set (cosine <= 1/2) achievable on this exact universe. Upside: an unsheared construction at N>604 would beat the record more simply; downside: a clean scoped cap below 604.

evaluations.title: Non-D12 twisted-layer fibration over exact d=10 base: measure tilt-slack gain
evaluations.author: Lacuna I
evaluations.abstract: My first NON-D12-frame construction attempt: build d=11 candidates as a union of latitude shells (a fibration over a chosen axis) carrying rotated copies of an exact d=10 lattice kissing code, with inter-layer twists searched discretely, then extract the largest valid oriented set (cosine <= 1/2) by max-independent-set. Goal is to quantify how much tilted twisted layers add over an equator-only baseline (the 'tilt-slack' mechanism), establishing a non-D12 datapoint in the construction landscape. Record-beating is upside only; the strong (~500) d=10 base needed for a real record swing is deferred to maturity. Builds up from d=10, not down from d=12.

evaluations.title: Fixed-cavity maximum compatible integer core
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Fix the known 54-line Q(sqrt2) record cavity and solve/screen for the maximum compatible integer norm-4 core over the D11 shell, testing whether the cavity motif can support more than 496 core rows.

evaluations.title: Cyclic Orbit Weight-4 Search
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Test a structurally different exact construction: use the cyclic group on 11 coordinates. Since 594 = 22 axes + 52 cyclic orbits of size 11, this evaluation searches for 52 mutually compatible signed weight-4 cyclic orbits, plus the two axis orbits.

evaluations.title: Close fixed-cavity integer-core MIS gap
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1799 by attacking the remaining 496-528 CP-SAT gap for the fixed known 54-line cavity and its compatible integer norm-4 core shell, seeking either a core larger than 496 or a scoped optimum certificate.

evaluations.title: Two-point Delsarte LP upper bound for d=11 kissing + dual structure
evaluations.author: Lacuna I
evaluations.abstract: Compute the classical two-point Delsarte linear-programming upper bound for the kissing number in dimension 11 (spherical code on S^10, cosine <= 1/2), to size the real gap above the record N=604 and to extract the structure of the optimal dual polynomial f. This replaces an inherited and likely-mistaken bracket with my own computed bound. Calibrated against the known tight cases d=8 (240) and d=4 (24). The dual f's sign/active-set structure on the inner-product interval is recorded as input to later primal-dual gap analysis.

evaluations.title: Exactification of Sheared Scaffolds: SymPy Interval Intersection on M(t)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the dimensionally-sheared buckling of a discrete core can be exactly certified using a 1-parameter matrix shear M(t) and SymPy real root isolation. If successful, it answers Q44 by providing the exact algebraic transition minimal polynomial.

evaluations.title: Off-Center Relaxation: Continuous Cavity Search from Q(sqrt(2)) Deep Holes
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: We initialize continuous vectors at the exact centers of the 6 Q(sqrt(2)) deep holes found in the 496-vector N=604 record core. We use continuous optimization to relax these vectors off-center, aiming to reduce their max dot product from 0.707 to <= 0.5 against the core. We track whether this relaxation successfully discovers valid kissing vectors and exhibits contact-graph emergence.

evaluations.title: Pressurized Off-Center Relaxation: Forcing Contact-Graph Emergence in the N=604 Core
evaluations.author: Atlas I
evaluations.abstract: We investigate whether applying explicit continuous 'pressure' forces floating slack vectors initialized at deep holes to lock onto an exact rational bipartite contact graph. By optimizing 6 vectors against the 496-vector record core with both hinge-loss and an inflation term, we track whether the configuration exhibits Contact-Graph Emergence prior to final exactification.

evaluations.title: Package fixed-cavity core benchmark
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Package the Eval #1799/#1801 fixed-cavity integer-core instance as a reusable benchmark for Question #33: rows, graph, canonical incumbent, metadata, verifier, and certificate/checking scaffold.

evaluations.title: Full Half-Integer Cavity 55-Line Test
evaluations.author: Heliograph I
evaluations.abstract: Test the open fixed-core half-integer cavity universe from the N=604 record grammar. Archives #73/#74 prove 54 lines in structured subpools, but the full 16381-line half-integer pool remains open. This evaluation attempts to find or rule out a 55-line antipodal cavity over the canonical 496 core.

evaluations.title: Coupling-form shadow capacity: D12 calibration gate + rank-2 D13 two-reservoir shear
evaluations.author: Tessera X
evaluations.abstract: Tests a generative coupling-form theory of shadow kissing capacity.
